DEN-MUSC-17FF-1.argument_summary: One unit of CPT 99214 on a single date cannot exceed frequency limits; the CARC 151/N362 denial is factually unsupported and should be reversed.
DEN-MUSC-17FF-1.letter_text:
RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Minh Monahan (MRN MUSC7419998), Claim MUSC-17FF-1

Patient: Minh Monahan  (DOB 2003-07-03)
MRN: MUSC7419998
Member ID / Group: BLU177743807 / GRP-38862
Claim number: MUSC-17FF-1
Date of service: 2026-05-07
Procedure billed: CPT 99214 — Office/outpatient visit, established patient, moderate complexity
Primary diagnosis: J06.9 — Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified
Denied amount: $611.29
Denial code: CARC 151 / RARC N362 — Payer deems the information submitted does not support this many/frequency of services.
Appeal deadline: 2026-09-17

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health is submitting this first-level reconsideration on behalf of Minh Monahan (Member ID: BLU177743807, MRN: MUSC7419998) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-17FF-1 for services rendered on May 7, 2026, by Robert K. Lindqvist, MD (NPI 1314059687). BlueChoice HealthPlan of South Carolina denied the claim in full — $611.29 billed, $0.00 paid — citing CARC 151 and RARC N362, with the payer remark stating: "Units billed exceed the plan's allowable frequency for this service." We respectfully assert that this denial is not supported by the facts of the claim and request immediate reversal and payment at the contracted rate.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Minh Monahan is a 23-year-old male patient with an established and documented history of recurrent upper respiratory conditions, including chronic sinusitis (active, onset 2014), seasonal allergic rhinitis (active), and atopic dermatitis (active). His medical history reflects a pattern of ongoing respiratory and allergic disease management, and he carries active prescriptions for loratadine and an epinephrine auto-injector, consistent with his allergic profile. On May 7, 2026, Mr. Monahan presented to MUSC Health University Medical Center as an established outpatient patient and was evaluated by Dr. Lindqvist for an acute upper respiratory infection (J06.9). The encounter was billed as a single unit of CPT 99214, an office or outpatient visit for an established patient requiring moderate medical decision-making. One unit of one service was submitted.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial under CARC 151 and RARC N362 is factually inapplicable to this claim. Both codes pertain to situations in which the number of units or frequency of a service exceeds a plan-defined threshold. However, Claim MUSC-17FF-1 was submitted with exactly one unit of CPT 99214 for a single date of service. There is no duplication, no repeat billing within a short interval, and no multi-unit submission that could logically trigger a frequency-based denial. A single evaluation and management visit by an established patient with active, documented medical conditions does not constitute excessive utilization by any reasonable clinical or administrative standard.
CPT 99214 is a widely recognized, appropriate code for an established-patient outpatient visit involving moderate complexity. Mr. Monahan's active chronic conditions — including chronic sinusitis and seasonal allergic rhinitis — combined with an acute upper respiratory infection presenting on the date of service, support the medical necessity and complexity level assigned. The place of service (22 — On Campus Outpatient Hospital) and revenue code 0510 are consistent with the facility setting and service type. Nothing in the claim submission suggests a coding error, duplicate claim, or frequency violation.
We respectfully request that BlueChoice review the claim record in its entirety. If the denial was triggered by an automated frequency edit, we ask that a clinical reviewer confirm that only one unit of one service on one date of service was billed, and that no prior claim for the same service on the same date exists in the system. If a specific frequency limitation is being applied, we request that BlueChoice identify the applicable plan provision and the prior utilization data upon which the denial was based, so that any factual discrepancy may be resolved.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that BlueChoice HealthPlan of South Carolina reverse the denial of Claim MUSC-17FF-1 and reprocess the claim for payment at the contracted allowed amount of $310.50. Should additional clinical documentation or coding clarification be required to complete this review, please contact the MUSC Health Revenue Cycle department directly. This reconsideration is being submitted electronically via MIM in accordance with the plan's appeal procedures, within the appeal deadline of September 17, 2026.

DEN-MUSC-1B1C-1.argument_summary: A routine established-patient E/M visit for an 85-year-old with active coronary heart disease is not a prior-authorization service; the denial is unsupported and internally inconsistent.
DEN-MUSC-1B1C-1.letter_text:
RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Stanford Windler (MRN MUSC3801368), Claim MUSC-1B1C-1

Patient: Stanford Windler  (DOB 1941-08-06)
MRN: MUSC3801368
Member ID / Group: ABS330201565 / GRP-63437
Claim number: MUSC-1B1C-1
Date of service: 2026-06-07
Procedure billed: CPT 99214 — Office/outpatient visit, established patient, moderate complexity
Primary diagnosis: J06.9 — Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified
Denied amount: $554.11
Denial code: CARC 197 / RARC N54 — Precertification/authorization/notification/pre-treatment absent.
Appeal deadline: 2026-10-29

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health University Medical Center is submitting this first-level appeal on behalf of patient Stanford Windler (MRN: MUSC3801368, Member ID: ABS330201565) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-1B1C-1 for a moderate-complexity established-patient office visit (CPT 99214) rendered on June 7, 2026, by James H. Ferrell, MD (NPI 1992837465). The claim was denied by Absolute Total Care (Centene) on July 31, 2026, under CARC 197 and RARC N54, with the payer remark stating: "No prior authorization on file for the date of service billed." The total denied amount is $554.11. MUSC Health respectfully contends that this denial is inconsistent with applicable Medicaid managed care requirements governing prior authorization for routine outpatient evaluation and management services, and requests full reversal and payment at the allowed rate of $319.26.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Mr. Windler is an 85-year-old male with an extensive and well-documented chronic disease burden managed longitudinally at MUSC Health. His active conditions include coronary heart disease (I25.10), for which he carries prescriptions for simvastatin, amlodipine, nitroglycerin, and clopidogrel — all initiated in May 2014 and currently active. He also carries active diagnoses of osteoporosis, gout, anemia, prediabetes, and obesity, as well as a longstanding history of chronic sinusitis dating to 1952. The June 7, 2026 encounter was billed under primary diagnosis J06.9 (acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified) with secondary diagnosis I25.10 (coronary heart disease), reflecting the complexity of managing an acute presentation in the context of significant underlying cardiovascular and metabolic comorbidities. Dr. Ferrell is the rendering provider and an established treating physician for this patient within the MUSC Health system.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial under CARC 197 and RARC N54 asserts that no prior authorization was on file for the date of service. MUSC Health disputes this characterization on two grounds.
First, under federal Medicaid managed care regulations and widely recognized standards applicable to Medicaid MCOs, routine outpatient evaluation and management visits — particularly for established patients presenting with acute illness — are generally not subject to prior authorization requirements. CPT code 99214 represents a standard office visit, not a procedure, specialty service, or high-cost intervention that would ordinarily trigger a precertification obligation. If Absolute Total Care's plan documents impose a prior authorization requirement on established-patient E/M visits at this level of complexity, MUSC Health requests that the payer identify the specific contractual or plan provision that mandates such authorization, as this requirement is not consistent with standard Medicaid managed care practice and may not have been communicated to network providers through the standard credentialing and contract notification process.
Second, even if a prior authorization obligation existed, denial under RARC N54 — indicating that claim information is inconsistent with pre-certified services — presupposes that some authorization was sought or issued. The payer's own remark states that no authorization is on file, which is logically inconsistent with the application of N54. This coding discrepancy further undermines the basis for denial and suggests the claim may have been processed in error.
Mr. Windler's active cardiovascular medications, his age, and the complexity of his comorbid conditions fully support the medical necessity of a moderate-complexity evaluation and management visit. The services rendered were appropriate, medically necessary, and consistent with the standard of care for an 85-year-old patient with coronary heart disease presenting with an acute upper respiratory condition.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that Absolute Total Care (Centene) reverse the denial of Claim MUSC-1B1C-1 in its entirety and issue payment at the contracted allowed amount of $319.26 for CPT 99214 rendered on June 7, 2026. If the payer maintains that prior authorization was required, we further request that Absolute Total Care provide, in writing, the specific plan provision or provider communication establishing that requirement, along with the retroactive authorization process available under applicable Medicaid managed care appeal rights. This appeal is submitted within the 90-day dispute window, ahead of the October 29, 2026 deadline, through the secure provider portal with supporting documentation attached.

DEN-MUSC-1B1C-2.argument_summary: One unit of CPT 99214 on a single date cannot exceed frequency limits; the denial under CARC 151/RARC N362 is factually inapplicable and should be reversed.
DEN-MUSC-1B1C-2.letter_text:
RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Stanford Windler (MRN MUSC3801368), Claim MUSC-1B1C-2

Patient: Stanford Windler  (DOB 1941-08-06)
MRN: MUSC3801368
Member ID / Group: ABS330201565 / GRP-63437
Claim number: MUSC-1B1C-2
Date of service: 2026-06-22
Procedure billed: CPT 99214 — Office/outpatient visit, established patient, moderate complexity
Primary diagnosis: J06.9 — Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified
Denied amount: $569.26
Denial code: CARC 151 / RARC N362 — Payer deems the information submitted does not support this many/frequency of services.
Appeal deadline: 2026-10-21

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health is submitting this first-level appeal on behalf of Stanford Windler (Member ID: ABS330201565, MRN: MUSC3801368, Date of Birth: August 6, 1941) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-1B1C-2 for services rendered on June 22, 2026, at MUSC Health Rutledge Tower Ambulatory Care. The claim was submitted on June 28, 2026, and denied by Absolute Total Care on July 23, 2026. The denied service is one unit of CPT 99214, an established patient office visit of moderate complexity, billed at $569.26. The payer denied the claim in full under CARC 151 ("Payer deems the information submitted does not support this many/frequency of services") and RARC N362 ("The number of days or units of service exceeds our acceptable maximum"), with the accompanying remark: "Units billed exceed the plan's allowable frequency for this service." MUSC Health respectfully disputes this denial. Only one unit of CPT 99214 was billed for a single face-to-face encounter on a single date of service, and a frequency-based denial is not applicable under these circumstances.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Mr. Windler is an 85-year-old male with a complex, longstanding medical history managed at MUSC Health. His active conditions include coronary heart disease (I25.10), for which he carries prescriptions for simvastatin, amlodipine, nitroglycerin, and clopidogrel — all initiated in 2014 and currently active. He also carries active diagnoses of osteoporosis, gout, anemia, prediabetes, and obesity, and has a documented history of chronic sinusitis dating to 1952. The June 22, 2026, encounter was conducted by Dr. Elena V. Castellanos, MD (NPI 1881726354) in the on-campus outpatient hospital setting (Place of Service 22). The primary diagnosis for this visit was acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified (J06.9), with coronary heart disease (I25.10) coded as a secondary diagnosis — a clinically appropriate pairing given Mr. Windler's active cardiac medication regimen and the need to assess any respiratory illness in the context of underlying cardiovascular disease. The level of service, CPT 99214, reflects moderate complexity consistent with the management of an acute condition overlaid on multiple chronic, active comorbidities in an elderly patient.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial rationale — that the number of units or frequency of service exceeds the plan's allowable maximum — is factually inapplicable to this claim. CPT 99214 was billed as one unit for one discrete outpatient encounter on June 22, 2026. A single evaluation and management service rendered on a single date of service cannot, by definition, constitute an excess frequency of that service on that date. CARC 151 and RARC N362 are appropriate when a provider submits multiple units of a service that is limited to one occurrence per day or per period, or when the same service is billed redundantly across overlapping claims. Neither circumstance applies here. The claim history in the case record does not reflect any other claim for CPT 99214 submitted for Mr. Windler on June 22, 2026, nor does the denial notice identify a conflicting claim or a specific frequency limit that this single unit allegedly exceeds. The denial therefore lacks a factual or coding basis. Furthermore, given Mr. Windler's age, active coronary heart disease, and multiple chronic conditions, an established-patient moderate-complexity visit is not only appropriate but represents the standard of care for managing an acute illness in a medically complex geriatric patient.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that Absolute Total Care conduct a complete review of this appeal, reverse the denial of Claim MUSC-1B1C-2, and issue payment at the allowed amount of $316.02 for the single unit of CPT 99214 rendered on June 22, 2026. Should the plan require additional clinical documentation, operative notes, or a peer-to-peer review with Dr. Castellanos, MUSC Health is prepared to provide those materials promptly through the secure provider portal in advance of the appeal deadline of October 21, 2026. We ask that this matter be resolved without further delay, as the service was medically necessary, correctly coded, and submitted in a timely and complete manner.

DEN-MUSC-1B1C-3.argument_summary: A standard outpatient E&M visit for an 85-year-old with active coronary disease cannot be excluded as non-covered when the payer's own remittance reflects an allowed amount for the same service.
DEN-MUSC-1B1C-3.letter_text:
RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Stanford Windler (MRN MUSC3801368), Claim MUSC-1B1C-3

Patient: Stanford Windler  (DOB 1941-08-06)
MRN: MUSC3801368
Member ID / Group: ABS330201565 / GRP-63437
Claim number: MUSC-1B1C-3
Date of service: 2026-05-22
Procedure billed: CPT 99214 — Office/outpatient visit, established patient, moderate complexity
Primary diagnosis: J06.9 — Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified
Denied amount: $568.93
Denial code: CARC 96 / RARC N130 — Non-covered charge(s).
Appeal deadline: 2026-10-02

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health Florence Medical Center is submitting this formal first-level appeal on behalf of patient Stanford Windler (MRN: MUSC3801368, Member ID: ABS330201565) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-1B1C-3 for services rendered on May 22, 2026. The claim was denied under CARC 96 (Non-covered charge(s)) with RARC N130, accompanied by the payer remark: "Service is excluded under the member's plan benefit document." MUSC Health respectfully disputes this determination. The service at issue — a Level 4 established patient office visit (CPT 99214) — represents a medically necessary, covered outpatient evaluation for an 85-year-old patient with multiple active chronic conditions, and the denial does not appear to be supported by the clinical facts or the applicable terms of the member's Absolute Total Care PPO plan.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Mr. Windler is an 85-year-old male with an extensive and active chronic disease burden, including coronary heart disease (I25.10), chronic sinusitis, osteoporosis, gout, anemia, prediabetes, and obesity. He carries active prescriptions for cardiovascular medications including simvastatin, amlodipine, nitroglycerin, and clopidogrel, reflecting the ongoing medical management required for his coronary artery disease. On May 22, 2026, Mr. Windler presented to MUSC Health Florence Medical Center, an on-campus outpatient hospital facility (Place of Service 22), under the care of rendering provider James H. Ferrell, MD (NPI 1992837465). The encounter was billed as CPT 99214, an established patient office or outpatient visit of moderate complexity, with a primary diagnosis of acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified (J06.9), and a secondary diagnosis of coronary heart disease (I25.10). Given the patient's age, active cardiovascular disease, and polypharmacy regimen, evaluation of an acute respiratory illness in this clinical context appropriately supports the moderate complexity level assigned.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial characterizes CPT 99214 as a non-covered service excluded under the member's plan benefit document. MUSC Health respectfully requests that Absolute Total Care identify with specificity the plan exclusion upon which this determination rests. Routine outpatient evaluation and management services for established patients are among the most fundamental benefits provided under Medicaid managed care plans and are not customarily subject to categorical exclusion. The member's coverage period runs from January 1, 2024, through December 31, 2026, and was active at the time of service. The claim was submitted on June 6, 2026, well within timely filing requirements, and this appeal is being submitted in advance of the October 2, 2026, appeal deadline.
CPT 99214 is a standard, widely recognized evaluation and management code. Its assignment here is consistent with the documented complexity of this patient's presentation: an acute illness overlaid on active coronary heart disease requiring ongoing antiplatelet and antianginal therapy. The payer's remittance acknowledges an allowed amount of $425.02, which itself implies the service falls within a recognized fee schedule — an acknowledgment that is difficult to reconcile with a claim that the service is wholly excluded from coverage. MUSC Health requests that Absolute Total Care reconcile this inconsistency and reconsider the denial in light of the full clinical and administrative record.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that Absolute Total Care (Centene) reverse the denial of Claim MUSC-1B1C-3 and reprocess the claim for payment at the previously established allowed amount of $425.02, or at the contractually applicable rate. Should the plan maintain that a specific benefit exclusion applies, MUSC Health requests that the plan provide the precise exclusion language and the section of the benefit document upon which it relies, so that this matter may be further reviewed or escalated as appropriate. MUSC Health is committed to resolving this matter through the plan's established dispute resolution process and appreciates Absolute Total Care's prompt attention to this appeal.

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health is submitting this formal first-level appeal on behalf of Kermit Trantow (Member ID: MOL620365519, MRN: MUSC5629233, Date of Birth: June 21, 1993) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-1F45-1 for services rendered on May 21, 2026, by Elena V. Castellanos, MD (NPI 1881726354) at MUSC Health University Medical Center. Molina Healthcare of South Carolina denied the claim under CARC 50 ("These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer") with RARC N115, citing a Local Coverage Determination, and further stated that "documentation submitted does not establish that the service was reasonable and necessary for the diagnosis reported." MUSC Health respectfully disagrees with this determination and requests full reversal and payment at the allowed amount of $289.80.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Mr. Trantow is a 33-year-old male with an established and documented medical history that includes active hypertension managed with Hydrochlorothiazide 25 MG, as well as a history of recurrent viral sinusitis with prior episodes recorded in 2014, 2017, and 2020. He also carries active prescriptions for Loratadine and an Epinephrine auto-injector, reflecting ongoing management of allergic and anaphylactic risk. The May 21, 2026 encounter was billed as CPT 99214, an established patient office visit of moderate complexity, with a primary diagnosis of J06.9 (Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified) and a secondary diagnosis of R69. The visit was conducted in an on-campus outpatient hospital setting (Place of Service 22), consistent with Mr. Trantow's established care relationship at MUSC Health.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial of medical necessity for this encounter is not supported by the clinical record. CPT 99214 reflects a moderate-complexity evaluation and management service for an established patient. Mr. Trantow's presentation with an acute upper respiratory infection must be considered in the context of his active comorbidities. His longstanding hypertension, currently managed pharmacologically, requires clinical consideration when evaluating and treating any acute illness, as certain common treatments for upper respiratory infections may interact with or affect blood pressure management. Additionally, his active prescriptions for an epinephrine auto-injector and loratadine indicate ongoing allergic risk that warrants careful clinical differentiation between an acute infectious process and an allergic exacerbation — a distinction that requires the level of medical decision-making consistent with a 99214 service level. The history of recurrent sinusitis further supports the clinical appropriateness of a thorough evaluation rather than a lower-acuity encounter. The payer's assertion that documentation does not establish medical necessity does not account for the complexity introduced by these concurrent active conditions. Evaluation and management of an acute upper respiratory illness in a patient with active hypertension and documented allergic risk constitutes a medically necessary service under any generally accepted standard of care. MUSC Health requests that Molina Healthcare reconsider the denial in light of the full clinical picture presented in the medical record.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that Molina Healthcare of South Carolina overturn the medical necessity denial for Claim MUSC-1F45-1 and process payment at the previously determined allowed amount of $289.80 for CPT 99214 rendered on May 21, 2026. Should Molina Healthcare require additional clinical documentation to support this determination, MUSC Health is prepared to provide the complete encounter record upon request. This appeal is submitted within the 90-day appeal window, prior to the stated deadline of September 15, 2026, and MUSC Health respectfully requests a written determination in accordance with Molina Healthcare's applicable appeal response obligations.

Primary diagnosis: J06.9 — Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified
Denied amount: $588.25
Denial code: CARC 50 / RARC N115 — These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
Appeal deadline: 2026-09-23

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health submits this first-level provider appeal on behalf of Kermit Trantow (Member ID: MOL620365519, MRN: MUSC5629233, DOB: 1993-06-21) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-1F45-2 for a date of service of May 16, 2026. Molina Healthcare of South Carolina denied the claim in full — $588.25 billed — under CARC 50 ("These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer") and RARC N115 ("This decision was based on a Local Coverage Determination (LCD)"), with the accompanying remark that "Documentation submitted does not establish that the service was reasonable and necessary for the diagnosis reported." MUSC Health respectfully disagrees with this determination and requests reversal and payment at the allowed amount of $319.85.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Mr. Trantow is a 33-year-old male established patient with a documented history relevant to upper respiratory illness. His medical record reflects a recurring pattern of viral sinusitis, with prior episodes recorded in 2014, 2017, and 2020, all coded under J06.9. He carries an active diagnosis of hypertension (I10), for which he is maintained on Hydrochlorothiazide 25 MG. His medication list also includes active prescriptions for Loratadine and an Epinephrine auto-injector, consistent with his history of allergic conditions. He has a resolved history of childhood asthma and perennial allergic rhinitis with seasonal variation. This constellation of chronic and recurrent conditions establishes Mr. Trantow as a patient whose upper respiratory presentations require ongoing clinical evaluation and management by a qualified provider.
On May 16, 2026, Dr. Marcus T. Bledsoe, DO (NPI 1770615243), evaluated Mr. Trantow at MUSC Health Ashley River Tower, an on-campus outpatient hospital facility (Place of Service 22). The visit was billed as CPT 99214, an established patient office or outpatient visit of moderate complexity, under primary diagnosis J06.9 — Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
CPT 99214 is appropriately assigned to an established patient encounter requiring moderate medical decision-making or a medically appropriate history and examination with moderate complexity. Mr. Trantow's clinical profile supports this level of service. His active hypertension and ongoing medication management, combined with a recurrent history of viral sinusitis and active allergy-related prescriptions including an epinephrine auto-injector, create a clinical picture in which an acute upper respiratory infection carries meaningful management complexity. The treating physician was required to assess the acute presentation in the context of these comorbidities, evaluate for potential medication interactions or contraindications, and determine an appropriate treatment course — all factors consistent with moderate complexity decision-making.
The payer's denial rests on the assertion that the documentation does not establish medical necessity for the service as reported. However, an acute upper respiratory infection in a patient with active hypertension, a history of asthma, and current use of an epinephrine auto-injector is not a routine, self-limiting complaint that can be dismissed without clinical evaluation. The need for physician assessment is both clinically appropriate and consistent with generally accepted standards of care for established patients presenting with acute illness superimposed on chronic conditions. Molina Healthcare's own coverage obligations under its Medicaid managed care contract require that medically necessary covered services be authorized and reimbursed when documentation supports the clinical need.
MUSC Health requests that Molina Healthcare conduct a full clinical review of the submitted documentation in light of Mr. Trantow's complete medical history as outlined above, and that the denial be reversed accordingly.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that Molina Healthcare of South Carolina overturn the denial of Claim MUSC-1F45-2 and issue payment at the previously established allowed amount of $319.85 for CPT 99214 rendered on May 16, 2026. Should additional clinical documentation be required to complete this review, please contact MUSC Health Revenue Cycle Appeals at the information provided on the accompanying cover sheet. This appeal is submitted within the 90-day appeal window, prior to the stated deadline of September 23, 2026.

Appeal deadline: 2026-08-26

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health is submitting this formal first-level appeal on behalf of patient Stan Steuber (MRN: MUSC2381078, Member ID: ABS259528514) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-2547-1 for services rendered on May 5, 2026, at MUSC Health Ashley River Tower. The claim was denied by Absolute Total Care (Centene) under CARC 204 ("This service/equipment/drug is not covered under the patient's current benefit plan") and RARC N130 ("Consult plan benefit documents/guidelines for information about restrictions for this service"), with the payer remark stating: "Service is excluded under the member's plan benefit document." MUSC Health respectfully disputes this determination and requests full reimbursement of the billed amount of $482.65 for CPT code 99214.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Mr. Steuber is a 57-year-old male with an active diagnosis of hyperlipidemia (ICD-10 E78.5), documented as ongoing since December 2017. He has been maintained on simvastatin 10 mg, with the current active order placed at his January 2021 follow-up visit, at which time a total cholesterol of 206.17 mg/dL was recorded. His medical history also includes active obesity (ICD-10 E66.9, onset 2009), which is a recognized comorbidity relevant to cardiovascular risk management. The May 5, 2026 encounter, billed as a 99214 established outpatient visit of moderate complexity, was a follow-up visit for the ongoing management of his hyperlipidemia. The service was rendered by Dr. Sarah E. Whitmore, MD (NPI 1447382910) in an on-campus outpatient hospital setting (Place of Service 22), consistent with Mr. Steuber's established care pattern at MUSC Health.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial characterizing this evaluation and management service as a non-covered benefit is not consistent with standard Medicaid managed care coverage obligations. Outpatient office and clinic visits for the management of chronic conditions such as hyperlipidemia are among the most fundamental services covered under Medicaid benefit structures, and Absolute Total Care, as a Medicaid managed care organization operating under a state contract, is required to cover medically necessary outpatient services at a minimum. A routine follow-up visit for an active, chronic, and clinically significant condition does not constitute an excluded service under any standard Medicaid benefit framework.
Furthermore, CPT code 99214 was appropriately selected for this encounter. An established patient visit involving the ongoing management of active hyperlipidemia with a documented medication regimen and relevant comorbidities supports moderate medical decision-making, consistent with the requirements for this level of service under current CPT evaluation and management guidelines. The denial does not allege a coding error, and no clinical or coding rationale has been provided to support the exclusion finding beyond a general reference to the plan benefit document. MUSC Health requests that Absolute Total Care identify with specificity the benefit exclusion provision upon which this denial is based, as the payer's current explanation does not provide sufficient information to evaluate or rebut the stated basis for denial.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that Absolute Total Care (Centene) reverse the denial of Claim MUSC-2547-1 and issue payment at the allowed amount of $296.53, or at the applicable contracted rate, for CPT 99214 rendered on May 5, 2026. Should the plan maintain that a specific benefit exclusion applies, MUSC Health requests that the plan provide the precise contractual or benefit document language supporting that determination so that a complete response may be submitted. This appeal is being submitted in advance of the August 26, 2026 appeal deadline, through the secure provider portal as directed on the Explanation of Payment.

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health Florence Medical Center submits this first-level appeal on behalf of patient Stan Steuber (MRN: MUSC2381078, Member ID: ABS259528514) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-2547-2 for a date of service of June 17, 2026. The claim was submitted on June 30, 2026, and denied by Absolute Total Care (Centene) on August 3, 2026, under CARC 50 ("These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer") and RARC N115 ("This decision was based on a Local Coverage Determination (LCD)"), with the accompanying payer remark that "Documentation submitted does not establish that the service was reasonable and necessary for the diagnosis reported." MUSC Health respectfully disagrees with this determination and requests full reversal and payment at the allowed amount of $344.90.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Mr. Steuber is a 57-year-old male established patient with active diagnoses of hyperlipidemia (E78.5) and obesity (E66.9), currently managed with Simvastatin 10 mg. On June 17, 2026, he presented to MUSC Health Florence Medical Center, an on-campus outpatient hospital facility, for evaluation by rendering provider Daniel R. Okafor, MD (NPI 1558493021). The encounter was billed under CPT 99214, reflecting an office or outpatient visit for an established patient requiring moderate-complexity medical decision-making. The primary diagnosis recorded for the visit was J06.9, acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified. Mr. Steuber's medical history is notable for recurrent episodes of viral sinusitis, with prior occurrences documented in 2011, 2013, and 2018, establishing a pattern of upper respiratory illness in this patient.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial on medical necessity grounds is not supported by the clinical facts of this encounter. An acute upper respiratory infection is a common, symptomatic condition that routinely and appropriately prompts an in-person evaluation by a licensed physician. The presenting complaint — an acute infectious illness — is precisely the type of condition for which an established-patient office visit is both reasonable and necessary. CPT 99214 requires moderate-complexity medical decision-making, which is consistent with evaluating an acute illness in a patient who carries active comorbidities including hyperlipidemia and obesity and who is on ongoing pharmacotherapy. The presence of these chronic conditions increases the clinical complexity of any acute presentation, as the treating physician must assess potential interactions, contraindications, and the impact of the acute illness on the patient's overall health status.
The payer's reliance on RARC N115, citing a Local Coverage Determination, does not override the clinical reality that this visit addressed an acute symptomatic condition in an established patient with a documented history of recurrent upper respiratory illness. The diagnosis of J06.9 is clinically appropriate and consistent with the patient's longitudinal history. MUSC Health maintains that the documentation supports the medical necessity of this service and that the denial reflects an overly restrictive application of coverage criteria to a straightforward, medically indicated encounter. Absolute Total Care's obligation under its provider agreement and applicable Medicaid managed care regulations requires that covered services be evaluated against accepted clinical standards, not denied on the basis of an unsupported assertion that necessity was not established.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that Absolute Total Care (Centene) reverse the denial of Claim MUSC-2547-2 and issue payment at the contracted allowed amount of $344.90 for CPT 99214 rendered on June 17, 2026. Should the plan require additional clinical documentation from Dr. Okafor's encounter record to complete its review, MUSC Health will provide that documentation promptly upon request. We ask that this appeal be adjudicated no later than the timeframes required under applicable Medicaid managed care appeal regulations. DEN-MUSC-2807-1.letter_text:
RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Trevor Turcotte (MRN MUSC0047531), Claim MUSC-2807-1

Patient: Trevor Turcotte  (DOB 1960-12-23)
MRN: MUSC0047531
Member ID / Group: BCB645769552 / GRP-83794
Claim number: MUSC-2807-1
Date of service: 2026-03-13
Procedure billed: CPT 99214 — Office/outpatient visit, established patient, moderate complexity
Primary diagnosis: J06.9 — Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified
Denied amount: $529.08
Denial code: CARC 27 / RARC N30 — Expenses incurred after coverage terminated.
Appeal deadline: 2026-08-07

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health is submitting this formal provider reconsideration on behalf of patient Trevor Turcotte (MRN: MUSC0047531, Member ID: BCB645769552, Group: GRP-83794) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-2807-1 for services rendered on March 13, 2026, at MUSC Health Ashley River Tower. BlueCross BlueShield of South Carolina denied the claim in full — $529.08 — citing CARC 27 ("Expenses incurred after coverage terminated") and RARC N30 ("Patient ineligible for this service"), with the payer remark stating, "Member was not eligible for benefits on the date of service billed." MUSC Health respectfully disputes this determination. The coverage record on file reflects an active BlueCross BlueShield of South Carolina Choice Plus plan with a coverage period of January 1, 2024, through December 31, 2026, which fully encompasses the March 13, 2026, date of service.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Mr. Turcotte is a 65-year-old male established patient with a documented history of active anemia (D64.9), prediabetes, and obesity, among other conditions. On March 13, 2026, he was evaluated by Amara J. Boone, NP (NPI 1203948576) in an on-campus outpatient hospital setting (Place of Service 22) at MUSC Health Ashley River Tower. The visit was billed as CPT 99214, an office or outpatient visit for an established patient of moderate complexity, with a primary diagnosis of acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified (J06.9), and a secondary diagnosis of anemia (D64.9). The claim was submitted timely on April 1, 2026, well within standard filing requirements.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The sole stated basis for denial is that Mr. Turcotte was not eligible for benefits on the date of service. However, the coverage documentation available to MUSC Health clearly reflects that the BlueCross BlueShield of South Carolina Choice Plus plan (Group GRP-83794, Member ID BCB645769552) carries an effective coverage period of January 1, 2024, through December 31, 2026. The date of service, March 13, 2026, falls squarely within that active coverage window. There is no indication in the information available to this facility that coverage was terminated, suspended, or otherwise interrupted prior to or on the date of service.
It is well established that a payer bears the responsibility of maintaining accurate and current eligibility data and of communicating any changes in member status to participating providers in a timely manner. If a retroactive termination occurred, MUSC Health was not notified of such action prior to rendering medically necessary care. Denying payment under these circumstances places an inequitable burden on both the provider and the patient. We respectfully request that BlueCross BlueShield of South Carolina review its internal eligibility records, including any retroactive adjustments, and provide specific documentation of the date and reason any alleged termination was processed.
The services rendered were medically appropriate for an established patient presenting with an acute upper respiratory condition in the context of active comorbidities including anemia and prediabetes, and were correctly coded and billed in accordance with CPT guidelines for a moderate-complexity outpatient encounter.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that BlueCross BlueShield of South Carolina conduct a thorough review of Mr. Turcotte's eligibility status as it existed on March 13, 2026, and reprocess Claim MUSC-2807-1 for payment at the applicable contracted rate. Should the payer's records reflect a discrepancy in eligibility, we request written documentation specifying the effective date of any termination and the basis for that action, so that the matter may be resolved appropriately. Enclosed with this reconsideration are the remittance advice reflecting the denial and supporting medical records for the date of service. This appeal is submitted in advance of the August 7, 2026, reconsideration deadline through My Insurance Manager (MIM) as directed.

DEN-MUSC-28D8-1.argument_summary: Denial lacks required specificity; colonoscopy is a recognized Medicaid-covered service supported by patient age, active comorbidities, and documented prior surveillance history.
DEN-MUSC-28D8-1.letter_text:
RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Sylvia Mitchell (MRN MUSC0887759), Claim MUSC-28D8-1

Patient: Sylvia Mitchell  (DOB 1948-10-21)
MRN: MUSC0887759
Member ID / Group: SCD721545870 / GRP-32400
Claim number: MUSC-28D8-1
Date of service: 2026-06-27
Procedure billed: CPT 45378 — Colonoscopy, flexible; diagnostic
Primary diagnosis: J06.9 — Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified
Denied amount: $2,891.42
Denial code: CARC 204 / RARC N130 — This service/equipment/drug is not covered under the patient's current benefit plan.
Appeal deadline: 2026-09-04

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health is submitting this formal appeal on behalf of patient Sylvia Mitchell (MRN: MUSC0887759, Member ID: SCD721545870) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-28D8-1 for services rendered on June 27, 2026, at MUSC Health University Medical Center. The claim was submitted on June 30, 2026, for CPT 45378 (colonoscopy, flexible; diagnostic), billed at $2,891.42, and was denied in full on August 5, 2026. South Carolina Medicaid (Healthy Connections / SCDHHS) issued the denial under CARC 204 — "This service/equipment/drug is not covered under the patient's current benefit plan" — with RARC N130 directing the provider to "consult plan benefit documents/guidelines for information about restrictions for this service," and a payer remark stating "Service is excluded under the member's plan benefit document." MUSC Health respectfully disputes this determination and requests full reconsideration and payment.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Ms. Mitchell is a 77-year-old female with an active coverage period under South Carolina Medicaid (Healthy Connections / SCDHHS) running from January 1, 2024, through December 31, 2026. Her documented active conditions include obesity (ICD-10 E66.9, onset 1992) and hyperlipidemia (ICD-10 E78.5, onset 1996), for which she has been maintained on Simvastatin 10 mg on a long-term basis. Her medical record reflects a prior colonoscopy performed on March 10, 2020, and an earlier colonoscopy on March 12, 2015, establishing a documented pattern of periodic colorectal surveillance. The June 27, 2026, procedure was performed by Marcus T. Bledsoe, DO (NPI 1770615243) in an on-campus outpatient hospital setting (Place of Service 22). Given Ms. Mitchell's age of 77 and her established history of prior colonoscopic examinations at clinically appropriate intervals, the performance of a diagnostic colonoscopy at this juncture is consistent with ongoing colorectal health monitoring in an elderly patient with relevant comorbidities.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial as issued is insufficiently specific to permit a meaningful response or correction. CARC 204 and the accompanying payer remark assert only that the service is "excluded under the member's plan benefit document," without identifying the specific exclusion provision, the benefit category at issue, or any clinical or administrative criterion that was not met. South Carolina Medicaid is obligated under federal Medicaid law and SCDHHS policy to provide a clear and adequate explanation of any adverse benefit determination, including the specific reason for denial and the applicable coverage provision. The denial notice as received does not satisfy that standard.
Furthermore, CPT 45378 — a diagnostic flexible colonoscopy — is a recognized and reimbursable procedure under Medicaid fee-for-service programs for medically appropriate indications. Ms. Mitchell's age, her active obesity diagnosis coded as the secondary diagnosis on this claim, and her documented history of prior colonoscopies in 2015 and 2020 collectively support the medical appropriateness of this service. The rendering provider, Dr. Bledsoe, determined that the procedure was warranted, and nothing in the case record suggests that the service was experimental, duplicative, or otherwise categorically excluded. MUSC Health requests that SCDHHS identify with specificity the exclusion being applied so that the clinical record can be evaluated against the correct standard. If the denial is based on a coding concern — such as the primary diagnosis of J06.9 (acute upper respiratory infection) — MUSC Health is prepared to work with the treating provider to clarify the clinical documentation and, if appropriate, submit a corrected claim reflecting the diagnosis most directly related to the indication for the colonoscopy.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that South Carolina Medicaid (Healthy Connections / SCDHHS) conduct a full review of this appeal and take one of the following actions: (1) reverse the denial and issue payment at the allowed amount of $1,615.36 as established by the payer's own adjudication; or (2) provide a detailed written explanation identifying the specific benefit exclusion provision applied, the clinical or administrative basis for its application to this claim, and the criteria that would need to be satisfied for the service to be covered, so that MUSC Health may respond with targeted supporting documentation. This appeal is being submitted within the 30-day appeal deadline of September 4, 2026, and MUSC Health requests a written determination in accordance with SCDHHS appeal timelines.

Procedure billed: CPT 99214 — Office/outpatient visit, established patient, moderate complexity

Denial code: CARC 16 / RARC N290 — Claim/service lacks information or has submission/billing error(s).

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health is submitting this formal first-level appeal on behalf of Marlin Kuphal (Member ID: TRI659593889, MRN: MUSC4410722, Date of Birth: August 11, 1941) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-3CE3-1 for services rendered on May 1, 2026, at MUSC Health East Cooper Medical Center in Mount Pleasant, South Carolina. The claim was denied on May 26, 2026, under CARC 16 / RARC N290, with the payer remark stating: "Claim cannot be adjudicated; required data element(s) are missing or invalid," specifically citing a missing, incomplete, or invalid rendering provider primary identifier. MUSC Health respectfully disputes this denial and submits that the rendering provider's National Provider Identifier (NPI) was valid and present at the time of submission, and requests immediate reprocessing and payment of the claim.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Mr. Kuphal is an 85-year-old established male patient with a documented history of chronic sinusitis with onset dating to 1977 and longstanding hypertension managed with Hydrochlorothiazide, active since 1959. On May 1, 2026, he presented to MUSC Health East Cooper Medical Center for an outpatient encounter billed under CPT 99214, representing an office or outpatient visit for an established patient of moderate complexity. The primary diagnosis recorded was J06.9 (Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified), with a secondary diagnosis of I10 (Essential hypertension). The visit was conducted by Elena V. Castellanos, MD, NPI 1881726354, at a place of service designated as 22 (On Campus Outpatient Hospital). The total billed amount was $440.71, against an allowed amount of $270.98. No payment was issued.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial under RARC N290 asserts that the rendering provider's primary identifier was missing, incomplete, or invalid. MUSC Health maintains that this characterization is incorrect. Dr. Elena V. Castellanos holds an active NPI of 1881726354, which is a valid Type 1 individual NPI registered in the National Plan and Provider Enumeration System (NPPES). This NPI was included on the claim as submitted on May 12, 2026. TRICARE and its contracted administrator, Humana Military, are required under HIPAA transaction and code set standards to accept a valid NPI as the primary provider identifier on electronic claims. If a data element was flagged as invalid during processing, MUSC Health respectfully requests that TRICARE East identify the specific field or format discrepancy that triggered the edit, as the provider information on file is accurate and verifiable through NPPES. No clinical or medical necessity issue has been raised by the payer; the sole stated basis for denial is an administrative data element concern, which is correctable and does not reflect any deficiency in the care provided or the appropriateness of the services billed. MUSC Health is prepared to resubmit a corrected claim if the payer can identify the precise formatting requirement that was not met, but notes that the NPI as submitted is valid on its face.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that TRICARE East (Humana Military) reopen and reprocess Claim MUSC-3CE3-1 in full, applying the allowed amount of $270.98 and issuing payment accordingly. Should the payer identify a specific data element or formatting deficiency that prevented adjudication, we request written notification of that deficiency so that a corrected claim may be submitted without delay. This appeal is being filed within the 90-day appeal window, prior to the stated deadline of August 24, 2026. MUSC Health remains committed to resolving this matter promptly and cooperatively, and asks that the payer provide a written determination in accordance with TRICARE's applicable appeal response timeframe requirements.

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health Florence Medical Center submits this formal first-level appeal on behalf of Marlin Kuphal (Member ID: TRI659593889) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-3CE3-2, covering services rendered on April 13, 2026 by Daniel R. Okafor, MD (NPI 1558493021). The claim was submitted on April 25, 2026 for CPT code 99214 (office/outpatient visit, established patient, moderate complexity, two units) under revenue code 0510 at MUSC Health Florence Medical Center, an on-campus outpatient hospital setting. The total billed amount of $1,196.45 was denied in full, with $0.00 paid against an allowed amount of $679.27. This appeal is submitted within the 90-day filing window prior to the August 13, 2026 deadline.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Mr. Kuphal is an 85-year-old male with an established and documented medical history relevant to the services billed on the date of service. His active conditions include chronic sinusitis with onset dating to 1977 and hypertension with onset dating to 1959, for which he has been maintained on Hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg as an active, long-standing medication. His medical record further reflects a recurrent pattern of acute upper respiratory conditions, including prior episodes of viral sinusitis and acute viral pharyngitis documented across multiple years. The primary diagnosis reported on the claim, J06.9 (Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified), is consistent with this established clinical history. The secondary diagnosis of I10 (Essential hypertension) reflects his active, chronic comorbidity requiring ongoing management. The payer's remark further states that "documentation submitted does not establish that the service was reasonable and necessary for the diagnosis reported."

DEN-MUSC-3CE3-3.argument_summary: Active TRICARE East coverage through 12/31/2026 encompasses the 6/6/2026 date of service; CARC 27 denial is unsupported and should be reversed.
DEN-MUSC-3CE3-3.letter_text:
RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Marlin Kuphal (MRN MUSC4410722), Claim MUSC-3CE3-3

Patient: Marlin Kuphal  (DOB 1941-08-11)
MRN: MUSC4410722
Member ID / Group: TRI659593889 / GRP-81211
Claim number: MUSC-3CE3-3
Date of service: 2026-06-06
Procedure billed: CPT 99214 — Office/outpatient visit, established patient, moderate complexity
Primary diagnosis: J06.9 — Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified
Denied amount: $1,082.64
Denial code: CARC 27 / RARC N30 — Expenses incurred after coverage terminated.
Appeal deadline: 2026-10-14

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health is submitting this formal first-level appeal on behalf of patient Marlin Kuphal (MRN: MUSC4410722, Member ID: TRI659593889) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-3CE3-3 for services rendered on June 6, 2026, at MUSC Health University Medical Center, Charleston, SC. The claim was denied on July 16, 2026, under CARC 27 ("Expenses incurred after coverage terminated") and RARC N30 ("Patient ineligible for this service"), with the payer remark stating: "Member was not eligible for benefits on the date of service billed." MUSC Health respectfully disputes this determination. The patient's TRICARE East (Humana Military) Advantage coverage is documented as active from January 1, 2024, through December 31, 2026, which encompasses the June 6, 2026, date of service. The denial therefore appears to reflect an administrative eligibility discrepancy rather than an actual lapse in coverage.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Marlin Kuphal is an 85-year-old male with an established history of care, presenting on June 6, 2026, to an on-campus outpatient hospital setting (Place of Service 22) under the care of rendering provider Marcus T. Bledsoe, DO (NPI 1770615243). The visit was billed as CPT 99214, an office or outpatient visit for an established patient of moderate complexity, with two units submitted under revenue code 0510. The primary diagnosis was J06.9 (Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified), consistent with Mr. Kuphal's longstanding history of recurrent upper respiratory conditions including chronic sinusitis with onset dating to 1977. A secondary diagnosis of I10 (Essential hypertension) was also documented, reflecting a condition active since 1959 and currently managed with Hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg. The complexity of managing an acute respiratory presentation in the context of longstanding chronic sinusitis and hypertension in an 85-year-old patient is consistent with the moderate complexity level assigned to this encounter.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The sole stated basis for denial is that Mr. Kuphal was not eligible for benefits on the date of service. However, the coverage record on file with MUSC Health clearly reflects an active TRICARE East (Humana Military) Advantage plan under Group GRP-81211, with a coverage period of January 1, 2024, through December 31, 2026. The date of service, June 6, 2026, falls squarely within this verified coverage window. MUSC Health confirmed eligibility through standard verification processes prior to rendering services, and no notification of termination or interruption of coverage was received before or at the time of the encounter. A denial under CARC 27 is appropriate only when coverage has genuinely lapsed; where active coverage exists spanning the date of service, the denial is inconsistent with the facts of record. TRICARE beneficiaries retain appeal rights under applicable federal regulations governing military health benefits, and payers are obligated to adjudicate claims in accordance with verified eligibility data. MUSC Health respectfully requests that TRICARE East conduct a thorough review of Mr. Kuphal's eligibility records for June 6, 2026, and reconcile any discrepancy between its internal system and the coverage documentation on file.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health requests that TRICARE East (Humana Military) reverse the denial of Claim MUSC-3CE3-3 and reprocess the claim for payment in accordance with the contracted allowed amount of $807.84. Should the payer's eligibility system reflect a termination date that conflicts with the coverage period documented in this appeal, MUSC Health requests that the payer identify the specific source of that discrepancy and provide written clarification so that it may be resolved promptly. If additional documentation of Mr. Kuphal's enrollment status is required, MUSC Health will cooperate fully in obtaining and submitting that information. This appeal is being submitted within the 90-day appeal filing window, prior to the October 14, 2026, deadline.

DEN-MUSC-4D58-1.argument_summary: A 99214 for an acute illness in a patient with active insulin-dependent diabetic renal disease and CKD meets medical necessity; denial ignores documented clinical complexity.
DEN-MUSC-4D58-1.letter_text:
RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Lakendra Roberts (MRN MUSC6727789), Claim MUSC-4D58-1

Patient: Lakendra Roberts  (DOB 1962-07-26)
MRN: MUSC6727789
Member ID / Group: CIG406449781 / GRP-50704
Claim number: MUSC-4D58-1
Date of service: 2025-12-21
Procedure billed: CPT 99214 — Office/outpatient visit, established patient, moderate complexity
Primary diagnosis: J06.9 — Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified
Denied amount: $429.02
Denial code: CARC 50 / RARC N115 — These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
Appeal deadline: 2026-08-02

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health Florence Medical Center submits this first-level appeal on behalf of patient Lakendra Roberts (MRN: MUSC6727789, Member ID: CIG406449781, Group: GRP-50704) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-4D58-1 for services rendered on December 21, 2025, by Elena V. Castellanos, MD (NPI 1881726354). Cigna Healthcare denied the claim in full — $429.02 billed — under CARC 50 ("These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer") and RARC N115 ("This decision was based on a Local Coverage Determination (LCD)"), with the payer remark stating that "documentation submitted does not establish that the service was reasonable and necessary for the diagnosis reported." MUSC Health respectfully disagrees with this determination and requests full reversal and payment at the contracted allowed amount of $319.30.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Ms. Roberts is a 64-year-old female with a well-documented, longstanding history of complex chronic conditions managed at MUSC Health. Her active problem list includes chronic kidney disease, diabetic renal disease, hyperglycemia, prediabetes, metabolic syndrome, and anemia — conditions that have been continuously managed since at least 2001. She is maintained on active medications including long-term insulin therapy (Humulin 70/30, initiated 2003), extended-release metformin (initiated 2001), and hydrochlorothiazide (initiated 1995), reflecting the chronic and medically intensive nature of her ongoing care. Prior laboratory findings document a markedly elevated microalbumin-to-creatinine ratio and a significantly reduced estimated glomerular filtration rate, consistent with progressive renal involvement in the setting of her diabetic and metabolic conditions. The December 21, 2025 encounter was billed as CPT 99214 — an established outpatient visit of moderate complexity — with a primary diagnosis of J06.9 (acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified) and a secondary diagnosis of R69, which in this patient's record maps to her active conditions of hyperglycemia and metabolic syndrome.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial rests on the assertion that the visit was not medically necessary for the diagnosis reported. This conclusion is not supported by the clinical context. Ms. Roberts is an established patient with multiple active chronic conditions, including insulin-dependent diabetic renal disease and chronic kidney disease, that require ongoing monitoring and management. An acute upper respiratory illness in a patient of this complexity warrants evaluation at the level of moderate medical decision-making, as intercurrent illness in patients with compromised renal function and glucose dysregulation carries meaningful clinical risk. The selection of CPT 99214 is consistent with CPT coding guidelines for established outpatient visits requiring moderate complexity decision-making, which encompasses the assessment of an acute problem against the backdrop of multiple chronic conditions with potential for complications. The secondary diagnosis code R69 further reflects the active comorbid conditions present at the encounter. Cigna's reliance on an LCD to deny this service does not account for the totality of the patient's clinical picture, and the denial appears to evaluate the primary diagnosis in isolation rather than in the context of the patient's established, medically complex profile.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health requests that Cigna Healthcare conduct a full clinical review of this appeal, including the complete medical record for the December 21, 2025 encounter and Ms. Roberts's longitudinal problem and medication history. Upon review, we request that the denial be reversed in full and that payment be issued at the contracted allowed amount of $319.30. Should Cigna require additional clinical documentation or a peer-to-peer review with Dr. Castellanos, we welcome that opportunity and ask that it be arranged promptly given the appeal deadline of August 2, 2026. This appeal is being submitted through the designated channel in accordance with Cigna's appeal process requirements.

DEN-MUSC-4D58-2.argument_summary: An ED visit (CPT 99284) for a medically complex patient with active CKD, insulin-dependent diabetes, and anemia is a covered emergency benefit, not a plan exclusion.
DEN-MUSC-4D58-2.letter_text:
RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Lakendra Roberts (MRN MUSC6727789), Claim MUSC-4D58-2

Patient: Lakendra Roberts  (DOB 1962-07-26)
MRN: MUSC6727789
Member ID / Group: CIG406449781 / GRP-50704
Claim number: MUSC-4D58-2
Date of service: 2026-06-02
Procedure billed: CPT 99284 — Emergency department visit, moderate-to-high severity
Primary diagnosis: J06.9 — Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified
Denied amount: $3,653.80
Denial code: CARC 96 / RARC N130 — Non-covered charge(s).
Appeal deadline: 2026-12-23

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health is submitting this first-level appeal on behalf of patient Lakendra Roberts (MRN: MUSC6727789, Member ID: CIG406449781, Group: GRP-50704) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-4D58-2 for services rendered on June 2, 2026, at MUSC Health University Medical Center. Cigna Healthcare denied the claim in full — billed charges of $3,653.80 — citing CARC 96 (Non-covered charge(s)) and RARC N130, with the payer remark stating: "Service is excluded under the member's plan benefit document." MUSC Health respectfully disputes this determination. The service at issue — CPT 99284, an emergency department evaluation and management visit of moderate-to-high severity — is a standard, widely covered benefit under commercial health plans, and the denial as stated does not withstand clinical or contractual scrutiny.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Ms. Roberts is a 64-year-old female with a documented history of complex, active chronic conditions including chronic kidney disease, diabetic renal disease, hyperglycemia, prediabetes, metabolic syndrome, and anemia. She is maintained on long-term insulin therapy (Humulin 70/30) and oral agents including Metformin and Hydrochlorothiazide. Her most recently recorded estimated glomerular filtration rate reflects significantly reduced kidney function, and her microalbumin-to-creatinine ratio has been persistently elevated across multiple measurements, indicating ongoing renal compromise. On June 2, 2026, Ms. Roberts presented to the MUSC Health University Medical Center Emergency Department, where she was evaluated by Elena V. Castellanos, MD (NPI 1881726354). The encounter was classified as an emergency visit with a primary diagnosis of acute upper respiratory infection (J06.9) and a secondary diagnosis coded to R69, which in the context of this patient's active conditions — including hyperglycemia and metabolic syndrome — reflects the complexity of her presentation. Given her underlying renal and metabolic disease burden, an acute infectious illness in this patient carries materially elevated clinical risk and appropriately warrants emergency-level evaluation.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
Cigna's denial categorizes CPT 99284 as a non-covered service excluded under the member's plan benefit document. However, emergency department evaluation and management services are among the most universally covered benefits under commercial health insurance, including Cigna Healthcare Choice Plus plans, and are specifically protected under longstanding federal and state prompt-access and coverage standards. MUSC Health requests that Cigna identify with specificity the plan exclusion language upon which this denial is based, as the denial notice itself provides no such citation beyond a general reference to the benefit document.
Furthermore, CPT 99284 was selected in accordance with the documented complexity of the encounter. Ms. Roberts's acute presentation must be evaluated in the context of her active chronic conditions, which include insulin-dependent diabetes with renal involvement, chronic kidney disease, and anemia — all of which elevate the medical decision-making complexity of any acute illness visit. The assignment of moderate-to-high severity is clinically supported by this patient's comorbidity profile. The claim was submitted correctly with appropriate diagnosis coding, place-of-service code 23, and revenue code 0450, all consistent with an emergency facility encounter.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that Cigna Healthcare conduct a full and impartial review of this appeal and overturn the denial of Claim MUSC-4D58-2. Specifically, we request that Cigna reprocess the claim and remit payment at the contracted allowed amount of $2,515.40, consistent with the plan's own adjudication of the allowable. In the event Cigna maintains its denial, we request a written explanation identifying the precise exclusion language in the member's benefit document that applies to emergency department evaluation and management services, as well as the clinical or contractual rationale for that determination. This appeal is submitted within the deadline of December 23, 2026, and includes supporting medical records for Cigna's review.

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health University Medical Center is submitting this formal appeal on behalf of patient Jonathan Hermiston (MRN: MUSC4336515, Member ID: AMB759343522) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-5214-1 for services rendered on June 9, 2026. Ambetter from Absolute Total Care denied the claim in full, citing CARC 204 ("This service/equipment/drug is not covered under the patient's current benefit plan") and RARC N130 ("Consult plan benefit documents/guidelines for information about restrictions for this service"), with the payer remark stating: "Service is excluded under the member's plan benefit document." The total denied amount is $4,860.97. MUSC Health respectfully contends that this denial is inconsistent with the nature of the service provided, the patient's documented clinical condition, and applicable coverage obligations under the Ambetter from Absolute Total Care Open Access plan, which carries an active coverage period through December 31, 2026.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Mr. Hermiston is a 78-year-old male with a complex, active medical history that includes Alzheimer's disease (onset October 2020), chronic obstructive bronchitis, hypertension, anemia, osteoarthritis of the knee, recurrent urinary tract infection, prediabetes, and a history of drug overdose. His Alzheimer's disease is actively managed with Galantamine 4 MG Oral Tablet, initiated in October 2020. His chronic obstructive bronchitis has been managed long-term with a fluticasone propionate/salmeterol combination inhaler, and he has undergone serial pulmonary rehabilitation and spirometry evaluations as recently as October 2020. The cumulative burden of these active, chronic conditions — particularly Alzheimer's disease in a 78-year-old patient — establishes a clear clinical basis for inpatient evaluation and management at the high-complexity level. The June 9, 2026 admission was billed under CPT 99223, initial hospital care at the highest level of medical decision-making complexity, rendered by Dr. Sarah E. Whitmore, MD (NPI 1447382910) at MUSC Health University Medical Center, an inpatient facility (Place of Service 21).

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial characterizes CPT 99223 as a non-covered or excluded service under Mr. Hermiston's benefit plan. This determination appears to be in error. CPT 99223 represents initial inpatient evaluation and management — a foundational category of physician services that is broadly covered under virtually all commercial and Marketplace health plans, including those offered under the Affordable Care Act. Marketplace plans are required to cover essential health benefits, which include hospitalization and physician services. A blanket exclusion of an initial inpatient hospital care code for a 78-year-old patient with active Alzheimer's disease and multiple serious comorbidities would be inconsistent with these coverage requirements. Furthermore, the plan's own allowed amount of $2,296.60 was calculated for this claim, which strongly suggests the service was recognized as a covered benefit at the adjudication level — making the simultaneous application of a non-covered denial internally contradictory. If the denial was triggered by a coding concern, MUSC Health notes that the primary diagnosis submitted, R69 (Illness, unspecified), may warrant review; however, the patient's documented active condition of Alzheimer's disease supports medical necessity for high-complexity inpatient care, and any coding discrepancy should result in a request for additional information rather than an outright non-covered denial.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that Ambetter from Absolute Total Care conduct a thorough review of this denial, reconcile the internally inconsistent application of a non-covered determination alongside a calculated allowed amount, and reprocess Claim MUSC-5214-1 for payment at the contracted rate. If the plan requires additional clinical documentation to support medical necessity or to clarify the primary diagnosis, MUSC Health will provide that documentation promptly upon request. This appeal is submitted in advance of the October 8, 2026 deadline through the secure provider portal as directed.

DEN-MUSC-6CD1-1.argument_summary: Acute E&M visit CPT 99214 for an unscheduled illness does not require prior authorization; denial under CARC 197/N54 should be reversed and the allowed amount paid.

Primary diagnosis: J06.9 — Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified
Denied amount: $590.37
Denial code: CARC 197 / RARC N54 — Precertification/authorization/notification/pre-treatment absent.
Appeal deadline: 2026-10-12

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health is submitting this formal appeal on behalf of Keitha Turner (Member ID: AMB999437436) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-6CD1-1 for services rendered on June 19, 2026, at MUSC Health East Cooper Medical Center. The claim was denied under CARC 197 ("Precertification/authorization/notification/pre-treatment absent") and RARC N54 ("Claim information is inconsistent with pre-certified/authorized services"), with the payer remark stating: "No prior authorization on file for the date of service billed." MUSC Health respectfully contests this denial and requests full reconsideration and payment of the allowed amount of $321.00.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Ms. Turner is a 22-year-old established patient who presented on June 19, 2026, for an outpatient office visit with Dr. Elena V. Castellanos, MD (NPI 1881726354) at MUSC Health East Cooper Medical Center. The visit was coded as CPT 99214, an office or outpatient visit for an established patient of moderate complexity, with a primary diagnosis of J06.9 (Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified). The service was rendered in a campus outpatient hospital setting (Place of Service 22, Revenue Code 0510). Ms. Turner has a documented clinical history relevant to her ongoing care, including prior episodes of acute viral pharyngitis, a history of subcutaneous immunotherapy, allergy screening, and active prescriptions including an epinephrine auto-injector and fexofenadine, indicating a background of allergic disease that contextualizes the complexity of her evaluation.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial of this claim on prior authorization grounds is not consistent with standard payer policy as it applies to evaluation and management services for acute, unscheduled conditions. CPT 99214 represents a medically necessary office visit for an established patient presenting with an acute upper respiratory infection. Acute, episodic outpatient evaluation and management visits of this nature are broadly recognized across the industry as services that do not require prior authorization, as they are neither elective procedures nor scheduled interventions that would afford the treating provider an opportunity to obtain precertification in advance. Requiring prior authorization for an unscheduled acute illness visit would be inconsistent with timely access-to-care obligations under applicable Marketplace plan requirements and standard managed care practice.
Furthermore, RARC N54 indicates that the claim information is inconsistent with pre-certified or authorized services. To the extent that no authorization was sought, this is because no authorization requirement applies to this category of service. The absence of an authorization on file does not constitute a clinical or administrative deficiency on the part of MUSC Health or the rendering provider; rather, it reflects the nature of the service itself. Dr. Castellanos appropriately documented and billed the encounter in accordance with CPT and ICD-10 guidelines. The billed charge of $590.37 and the payer's own allowed amount of $321.00 confirm that the service was recognized as a covered benefit — the sole basis for non-payment is the authorization issue, which MUSC Health submits is inapplicable here.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that Ambetter from Absolute Total Care reverse the denial of Claim MUSC-6CD1-1 and issue payment of the allowed amount of $321.00 for CPT 99214 rendered on June 19, 2026. Should the plan maintain that a prior authorization requirement applies to this service, we further request that the plan provide, in writing, the specific benefit provision or clinical policy that mandates precertification for unscheduled acute evaluation and management visits billed under CPT 99214 in an outpatient hospital setting. This appeal is submitted within the appeal deadline of October 12, 2026, through the secure provider portal as directed.

MUSC Health respectfully disputes this denial and requests full reimbursement of the billed amount of $511.02 for CPT code 99214, an established outpatient office visit of moderate complexity.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Ms. Turner is a 22-year-old established patient who presented on July 5, 2026, at the on-campus outpatient facility (Place of Service 22) for evaluation and management of an acute upper respiratory infection (ICD-10: J06.9). The visit was conducted by Amara J. Boone, NP (NPI 1203948576) and was billed as a single unit of CPT 99214, reflecting a moderate-complexity evaluation and management service for an established patient. Ms. Turner's medical history is notable for recurrent episodes of acute viral pharyngitis, a documented shrimp IgE elevation, active prescriptions including an epinephrine auto-injector and fexofenadine, and a prior course of subcutaneous immunotherapy, all of which underscore her status as an established patient with an ongoing clinical relationship at this facility. The July 5, 2026 encounter falls within her active coverage period under the Ambetter from Absolute Total Care Advantage plan (coverage period: 2024-01-01 to 2026-12-31).

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial of this claim on prior authorization grounds is not consistent with standard payer practice for routine outpatient evaluation and management services. CPT 99214 is a widely recognized evaluation and management code for established outpatient patients and, under the vast majority of commercial and Marketplace plan benefit structures, does not require prior authorization when rendered in an outpatient setting for an acute, non-elective condition such as an upper respiratory infection. Acute upper respiratory infections by their nature require timely clinical assessment and do not lend themselves to prospective authorization workflows. Requiring prior authorization for this category of service would create a barrier to medically necessary, time-sensitive care in a manner inconsistent with both the patient's plan benefits and generally accepted managed care standards.
Furthermore, RARC N54 indicates that the claim information is inconsistent with pre-certified or authorized services. MUSC Health respectfully notes that if Ambetter's records reflect a prior authorization associated with a different service type or date, this may represent an administrative discrepancy rather than a true absence of coverage eligibility. We request that Ambetter conduct a thorough review of Ms. Turner's benefit structure to confirm whether prior authorization is, in fact, a contractual requirement for outpatient established-patient E&M services under her specific plan, and if so, to identify any applicable waiver provisions for urgent or acute presentations.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that Ambetter from Absolute Total Care overturn the denial of Claim MUSC-6CD1-2 and process the claim for payment in accordance with Ms. Turner's contracted plan benefits. The allowed amount on file is $313.53, and we request that payment be issued accordingly, or that the claim be reprocessed at the applicable contracted rate if a different amount applies. Should Ambetter determine that additional information is required to complete this review, we ask that a specific written request be submitted through the secure provider portal prior to the appeal deadline of October 26, 2026, so that MUSC Health may respond in a timely manner.
