DEN-MUSC-B4EA-1.argument_summary: Denial stems from an incorrect diagnosis code on submission, not lack of medical necessity; correction to reflect Ms. Moore's active anemia diagnosis supports CPT 74177.
DEN-MUSC-B4EA-1.letter_text:
RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Regena Moore (MRN MUSC8962062), Claim MUSC-B4EA-1

Patient: Regena Moore  (DOB 1964-12-08)
MRN: MUSC8962062
Member ID / Group: SCD742523430 / GRP-85832
Claim number: MUSC-B4EA-1
Date of service: 2026-06-23
Procedure billed: CPT 74177 — CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
Primary diagnosis: J06.9 — Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified
Denied amount: $2,674.63
Denial code: CARC 11 / RARC M64 — The diagnosis is inconsistent with the procedure.
Appeal deadline: 2026-08-19

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health is submitting this formal first-level appeal on behalf of patient Regena Moore (MRN: MUSC8962062, Member ID: SCD742523430) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-B4EA-1 for services rendered on June 23, 2026, at MUSC Health University Medical Center. The claim was denied on July 20, 2026, under CARC 11 ("The diagnosis is inconsistent with the procedure") and RARC M64 ("Missing/incomplete/invalid other diagnosis"), with the payer remark stating: "The diagnosis code reported does not support the procedure billed." The total denied amount is $2,674.63. MUSC Health respectfully requests that South Carolina Medicaid (Healthy Connections / SCDHHS) reverse this denial and reprocess the claim for appropriate payment.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Ms. Moore is a 61-year-old female patient with active diagnoses including anemia (D64.9) and prediabetes (E11.9), both of longstanding duration. On June 23, 2026, she presented as an outpatient at MUSC Health University Medical Center, where rendering provider Amara J. Boone, NP (NPI 1203948576) ordered CPT 74177, a CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis with contrast. The claim was submitted on June 30, 2026, with J06.9 (Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified) listed as both the primary and secondary diagnosis code. The procedure was performed in an on-campus outpatient hospital setting under revenue code 0510.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial is well-founded with respect to the diagnosis code as submitted, and MUSC Health acknowledges that J06.9 — Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified — does not, on its face, provide clinical justification for a CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast. However, the denial reflects a coding deficiency rather than a lack of medical necessity for the procedure itself. The claim was submitted with an incomplete and clinically inaccurate primary diagnosis code that does not reflect the full picture of Ms. Moore's active conditions or the clinical indication that prompted the imaging order.
Ms. Moore carries active diagnoses of anemia (D64.9) and prediabetes (E11.9), both of which are documented in her longitudinal record. Additionally, her history includes a prior tubal pregnancy and a first-trimester miscarriage, conditions that are part of her gynecologic and abdominal history and may bear clinical relevance to abdominal and pelvic imaging. The presence of anemia, in particular, is a condition that can prompt evaluation of the abdomen and pelvis to investigate underlying etiology, and it represents a clinically supportable indication for the procedure performed. The submission of J06.9 as the sole diagnosis appears to be a coding error in which the appropriate diagnosis or diagnoses reflecting the true clinical indication were not captured on the claim.
Under correct coding principles consistent with ICD-10-CM guidance, the diagnosis reported on a claim must reflect the condition that prompted the service, not an unrelated or incidental condition. The failure to report the correct diagnosis code constitutes a correctable billing error, not a determination that the service was medically unnecessary. South Carolina Medicaid's appeal and claims correction processes recognize that coding errors are subject to review and correction upon submission of supporting documentation.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that South Carolina Medicaid (Healthy Connections / SCDHHS) review the complete medical record for the June 23, 2026, encounter, consider the active diagnoses documented in Ms. Moore's record — including anemia (D64.9) — as the clinically appropriate basis for the CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast, and either reprocess the claim with the corrected diagnosis coding or provide guidance to allow MUSC Health to submit a corrected claim. We further request that the allowed amount of $1,578.45 already established by the payer be honored upon reprocessing. All supporting clinical documentation is available upon request and will be submitted promptly to facilitate timely resolution prior to the August 19, 2026, appeal deadline.

DEN-MUSC-B4EA-2.argument_summary: A 99214 for an acute URI in a patient with active anemia and prediabetes meets medical necessity; the denial lacks a specific documentation deficiency and should be reversed.
DEN-MUSC-B4EA-2.letter_text:
RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Regena Moore (MRN MUSC8962062), Claim MUSC-B4EA-2

Patient: Regena Moore  (DOB 1964-12-08)
MRN: MUSC8962062
Member ID / Group: SCD742523430 / GRP-85832
Claim number: MUSC-B4EA-2
Date of service: 2026-06-28
Procedure billed: CPT 99214 — Office/outpatient visit, established patient, moderate complexity
Primary diagnosis: J06.9 — Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified
Denied amount: $428.70
Denial code: CARC 50 / RARC N115 — These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
Appeal deadline: 2026-09-04

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health University Medical Center is submitting this formal first-level appeal on behalf of patient Regena Moore (MRN: MUSC8962062, Member ID: SCD742523430) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-B4EA-2 for services rendered on June 28, 2026, by Dr. Marcus T. Bledsoe, DO (NPI 1770615243). South Carolina Medicaid (Healthy Connections / SCDHHS) denied the claim in full — billed charges of $428.70 — citing CARC 50 ("These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer") and RARC N115 ("This decision was based on a Local Coverage Determination (LCD)"), with the accompanying remark that "Documentation submitted does not establish that the service was reasonable and necessary for the diagnosis reported." MUSC Health respectfully disagrees with this determination and requests full reversal and payment at the allowed amount of $232.75.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Ms. Moore is a 61-year-old established female patient with active chronic conditions including anemia (D64.9, managed with ongoing ferrous sulfate therapy since 2001) and prediabetes (E11.9, onset 1998), both of which require periodic monitoring and clinical management. On June 28, 2026, she presented to MUSC Health University Medical Center's on-campus outpatient facility for an evaluation and management visit with Dr. Bledsoe, coded as CPT 99214 — an office or outpatient visit for an established patient involving moderate medical decision-making. The primary diagnosis recorded for this encounter was J06.9, acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified. Ms. Moore's longitudinal history reflects a pattern of recurrent acute respiratory illnesses, including prior episodes of acute bronchitis, viral pharyngitis, and viral sinusitis, as well as her active comorbidities, all of which are relevant to the clinical complexity of any acute presentation.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial rests on the assertion that the documentation does not establish medical necessity for the service as billed. MUSC Health contends that this determination is inconsistent with both the clinical facts of the encounter and the applicable standards governing evaluation and management services under South Carolina Medicaid.
CPT 99214 is appropriately assigned to an established patient visit involving moderate complexity, which encompasses the assessment of an acute illness with consideration of the patient's underlying chronic conditions. Ms. Moore's active diagnoses of anemia and prediabetes represent comorbid factors that a treating physician must reasonably consider when evaluating an acute upper respiratory infection, as these conditions can influence symptom presentation, treatment selection, and patient risk. The level of service billed reflects this clinical context and is consistent with generally accepted evaluation and management coding guidelines.
Furthermore, J06.9 is a recognized, billable ICD-10-CM diagnosis code for acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified, and its use does not in itself preclude a finding of medical necessity. An acute symptomatic illness in a patient with multiple active chronic conditions constitutes a medically necessary reason for an outpatient encounter. The payer has not identified a specific documentation deficiency beyond a general assertion, and MUSC Health maintains that the medical record supports the level and nature of service provided. Should the payer require additional clinical documentation from the treating provider, MUSC Health is prepared to submit supplemental records upon request.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that South Carolina Medicaid (Healthy Connections / SCDHHS) reverse the denial of Claim MUSC-B4EA-2 and reprocess the claim for payment at the applicable allowed amount of $232.75. This appeal is submitted within the 30-day appeal window, prior to the September 4, 2026 deadline. If the payer requires additional clinical documentation or a peer-to-peer review to support this determination, please contact MUSC Health's Revenue Cycle Appeals department at your earliest convenience so that we may facilitate a timely resolution.

DEN-MUSC-B85D-1.argument_summary: Denial under CARC 16/RARC N290 is unwarranted; rendering provider NPI 1881726354 is valid and reaffirmed here, and the claim should be reprocessed for payment.
DEN-MUSC-B85D-1.letter_text:
RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Twanda Rippin (MRN MUSC5789896), Claim MUSC-B85D-1

Patient: Twanda Rippin  (DOB 1973-01-28)
MRN: MUSC5789896
Member ID / Group: SCD540309134 / GRP-17900
Claim number: MUSC-B85D-1
Date of service: 2026-07-01
Procedure billed: CPT 99214 — Office/outpatient visit, established patient, moderate complexity
Primary diagnosis: D64.9 — Anemia, unspecified
Denied amount: $407.10
Denial code: CARC 16 / RARC N290 — Claim/service lacks information or has submission/billing error(s).
Appeal deadline: 2026-08-27

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health is submitting this formal appeal on behalf of patient Twanda Rippin (MRN: MUSC5789896, Member ID: SCD540309134) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-B85D-1, covering services rendered on July 1, 2026, at MUSC Health Ashley River Tower. The claim was denied on July 28, 2026, under CARC 16 and RARC N290, with the payer remark stating: "Claim cannot be adjudicated; required data element(s) are missing or invalid," citing a missing, incomplete, or invalid rendering provider primary identifier. MUSC Health respectfully disputes this denial and asserts that the rendering provider's National Provider Identifier (NPI) was valid and present on the original claim submission.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Ms. Rippin is a 53-year-old established female patient with active diagnoses of anemia, unspecified (D64.9), and chronic sinusitis (J06.9), both of which served as the basis for the July 1, 2026, outpatient encounter. Her anemia has been an active, documented condition since February 2017, and she has an ongoing treatment history that includes Vitamin B12 injectable solution. She is also being managed for prediabetes. The visit was billed as CPT 99214, an office or outpatient visit for an established patient requiring moderate-complexity medical decision-making, rendered by Dr. Elena V. Castellanos, MD, at place of service 22 (on-campus outpatient hospital). The billed amount was $407.10. The clinical appropriateness of the visit and the accuracy of the procedure and diagnosis codes are not in dispute; the sole stated basis for denial is an administrative data element issue.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial under RARC N290 indicates that the rendering provider's primary identifier — the NPI — was considered missing, incomplete, or invalid. MUSC Health maintains that Dr. Elena V. Castellanos, MD, holds a valid and active NPI (1881726354) and that this identifier was included on the claim as submitted on July 5, 2026. Under HIPAA administrative simplification standards and South Carolina Medicaid billing requirements, the NPI is the required primary identifier for rendering providers on professional and institutional claims, and Dr. Castellanos's NPI satisfies that requirement.
To the extent that a technical submission error caused the NPI to appear absent or unreadable during adjudication, this appeal serves as the vehicle to correct that administrative deficiency. South Carolina Medicaid's appeal and resubmission processes expressly permit correction of claim submission errors of this nature. The denial does not reflect any finding that the services were not medically necessary, not covered under the plan, or improperly coded. The allowed amount of $280.71 already established by the payer confirms that the service itself was recognized as a covered benefit; the sole impediment to payment is the unresolved provider identifier question, which this appeal directly addresses.
MUSC Health respectfully requests that South Carolina Medicaid treat this appeal as a corrected claim submission with the rendering provider NPI 1881726354 explicitly reaffirmed, and that the claim be reprocessed accordingly. All other claim data elements — including the member ID, date of service, place of service, procedure code, diagnosis codes, and billed charges — remain as originally submitted and are accurate.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health requests that South Carolina Medicaid (Healthy Connections / SCDHHS) reopen and reprocess Claim MUSC-B85D-1 using the confirmed rendering provider NPI 1881726354 for Dr. Elena V. Castellanos, MD, and issue payment at the applicable Medicaid allowed amount for CPT 99214 rendered on July 1, 2026. Should the payer require a formal corrected claim submission in addition to this appeal, MUSC Health is prepared to submit one immediately upon request. We ask that this matter be resolved within the timeframe required under South Carolina Medicaid's prompt-pay obligations and that written confirmation of the adjudication outcome be provided to MUSC Health's Revenue Cycle department.

DEN-MUSC-B898-1.argument_summary: Claim submitted 17 days post-service cannot be untimely; CARC 29 denial is factually unsupported and should be reversed with payment issued at the allowed amount.
DEN-MUSC-B898-1.letter_text:
RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Eduardo Treviño (MRN MUSC3540441), Claim MUSC-B898-1

Patient: Eduardo Treviño  (DOB 1971-02-01)
MRN: MUSC3540441
Member ID / Group: ABS836618976 / GRP-24383
Claim number: MUSC-B898-1
Date of service: 2026-06-08
Procedure billed: CPT 99214 — Office/outpatient visit, established patient, moderate complexity
Primary diagnosis: E78.5 — Hyperlipidemia, unspecified
Denied amount: $528.12
Denial code: CARC 29 / RARC N211 — The time limit for filing has expired.
Appeal deadline: 2026-10-14

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health is submitting this formal appeal on behalf of Eduardo Treviño (Member ID: ABS836618976) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-B898-1 for services rendered on June 8, 2026, by Dr. Elena V. Castellanos, MD (NPI 1881726354) at MUSC Health University Medical Center. The claim was denied by Absolute Total Care (Centene) on July 16, 2026, under CARC 29 ("The time limit for filing has expired") with accompanying remark RARC N211 ("You may not appeal this decision"), with the payer's stated basis being that the claim was received after the contractual filing deadline. MUSC Health respectfully disputes this denial and requests a full review and reversal, as the claim was submitted on June 25, 2026, well within any standard timely filing window measured from the June 8, 2026, date of service.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Mr. Treviño is a 55-year-old male with an active, longstanding diagnosis of hyperlipidemia (ICD-10 E78.5), documented as onset September 10, 2012. He has been managed continuously for this condition, with Simvastatin 10 mg ordered at regular annual intervals dating back to 2014, with the most recent active order placed on September 29, 2020. The June 8, 2026, encounter was a follow-up outpatient visit at MUSC Health University Medical Center (Place of Service 22) for ongoing management of his hyperlipidemia. The service was appropriately coded as CPT 99214, an established-patient office visit of moderate complexity, with a primary diagnosis of E78.5 and a secondary diagnosis of J06.9. The billed amount was $528.12, with a payer-allowed amount of $317.48 on file, confirming the service falls within covered benefits.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial under CARC 29 is factually unsupported. The date of service was June 8, 2026, and the claim was submitted to Absolute Total Care on June 25, 2026 — a span of only 17 days. Under any reasonable interpretation of standard Medicaid managed care contractual filing requirements, which commonly allow a minimum of 90 days and frequently up to 365 days from the date of service, a claim submitted 17 days post-service cannot be considered untimely. MUSC Health has no record of any notification from Absolute Total Care establishing a filing deadline shorter than 17 days, nor would such a requirement be consistent with applicable Medicaid managed care regulations or standard provider contract terms.
Furthermore, RARC N211 states that the denial may not be appealed. MUSC Health respectfully asserts that this remark does not extinguish the provider's right to dispute an erroneous denial. Appeal deadline: 2026-10-23

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health is submitting this formal first-level appeal on behalf of patient Eduardo Treviño (MRN: MUSC3540441, Member ID: ABS836618976) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-B898-2 for services rendered on June 27, 2026, at MUSC Health Ashley River Tower. The claim was denied by Absolute Total Care (Centene) on July 25, 2026, under CARC 18 ("Exact duplicate claim/service") and RARC N522 ("Duplicate of a claim processed or in process as a crossover/coordination of benefits claim"), with the payer remark stating: "Claim appears to duplicate a previously adjudicated claim." MUSC Health respectfully disputes this determination. The service in question represents a single, discrete, and independently documented outpatient encounter that has not been submitted, adjudicated, or paid under any prior claim.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
On June 27, 2026, Eduardo Treviño, a 54-year-old established male patient with an active diagnosis of hyperlipidemia (ICD-10 E78.5), presented to MUSC Health Ashley River Tower for an outpatient visit rendered by Robert K. Lindqvist, MD (NPI 1314059687). The encounter was billed under CPT 99214, reflecting an office or outpatient visit for an established patient of moderate complexity, with a primary diagnosis of acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified (ICD-10 J06.9). The claim was submitted on July 11, 2026, under place of service code 22 (On Campus Outpatient Hospital), revenue code 0510, for a billed amount of $758.95. This visit is clinically and temporally distinct from any prior encounter documented in Mr. Treviño's record.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The duplicate denial is not supported by the facts of this claim. A duplicate denial under CARC 18 and RARC N522 requires the existence of a previously adjudicated or in-process claim for the same patient, same date of service, same provider, and same procedure. MUSC Health has reviewed its billing records and confirms that Claim MUSC-B898-2 was submitted once, on July 11, 2026, for the June 27, 2026 date of service. No prior claim for this specific encounter has been submitted to Absolute Total Care or any other payer. The RARC N522 notation references a potential crossover or coordination of benefits scenario; however, the case record does not reflect any secondary payer involvement or crossover claim activity associated with this date of service that would give rise to such a characterization.
Furthermore, a review of Mr. Treviño's encounter history confirms that the most recent previously documented visit on file predates the June 27, 2026 encounter by a substantial period. There is no overlapping claim for the same date, provider, or procedure code that could reasonably support a duplicate determination. Denying a legitimately rendered and properly coded service on the basis of an unsupported duplicate finding results in an incorrect zero-payment outcome and is inconsistent with Medicaid managed care claims adjudication standards, which require payers to identify a specific prior claim before applying a duplicate denial.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that Absolute Total Care (Centene) reopen and reprocess Claim MUSC-B898-2 in full, applying the contracted allowed amount of $420.39 and issuing payment accordingly. We further request that the payer provide, in its response, the specific prior claim number alleged to be a duplicate of this submission, so that any discrepancy may be investigated and resolved promptly. Supporting documentation, including the claim submission record and encounter documentation for the June 27, 2026 visit, is attached for review. This appeal is submitted within the 90-day appeal window, prior to the October 23, 2026 deadline, through the secure provider portal as directed.

DEN-MUSC-B898-3.argument_summary: A 99214 E&M visit for acute URI in an established patient with active hyperlipidemia meets medical necessity; denial under CARC 50/RARC N115 is unsupported by clinical facts.
DEN-MUSC-B898-3.letter_text:
RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Eduardo Treviño (MRN MUSC3540441), Claim MUSC-B898-3

Patient: Eduardo Treviño  (DOB 1971-02-01)
MRN: MUSC3540441
Member ID / Group: ABS836618976 / GRP-24383
Claim number: MUSC-B898-3
Date of service: 2026-05-11
Procedure billed: CPT 99214 — Office/outpatient visit, established patient, moderate complexity
Primary diagnosis: J06.9 — Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified
Denied amount: $609.78
Denial code: CARC 50 / RARC N115 — These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
Appeal deadline: 2026-09-08

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health is submitting this first-level appeal on behalf of established patient Eduardo Treviño (MRN: MUSC3540441, Member ID: ABS836618976) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-B898-3 for services rendered on May 11, 2026, at MUSC Health University Medical Center. The claim was denied on June 10, 2026, under CARC 50 ("These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer") and RARC N115 ("This decision was based on a Local Coverage Determination (LCD)"), with the accompanying payer remark stating that "Documentation submitted does not establish that the service was reasonable and necessary for the diagnosis reported." MUSC Health respectfully disagrees with this determination and requests full reversal and payment of the billed amount of $609.78.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Mr. Treviño is a 55-year-old male with an active diagnosis of hyperlipidemia (E78.5, onset 2012), for which he has been maintained on simvastatin 10 mg with ongoing laboratory monitoring over multiple years. He presented on May 11, 2026, to an on-campus outpatient hospital setting (Place of Service 22) under the care of Robert K. Lindqvist, MD (NPI 1314059687) for evaluation and management of an acute upper respiratory infection (J06.9). The visit was coded as CPT 99214, reflecting an office or outpatient visit for an established patient with moderate complexity medical decision-making. Mr. Treviño has a documented history of recurrent upper respiratory conditions, including prior episodes of acute viral pharyngitis, viral sinusitis, and acute bronchitis, all previously coded under J06.9, establishing a relevant clinical pattern for this presentation.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial on medical necessity grounds is not supported by the clinical facts of this encounter. CPT 99214 is an appropriate and well-recognized evaluation and management code for an established patient presenting with an acute symptomatic illness. Acute upper respiratory infection (J06.9) is a legitimate, commonly treated diagnosis that warrants in-person physician evaluation, particularly in a patient with an active chronic condition such as hyperlipidemia and a history of recurrent respiratory illness. The selection of a moderate-complexity level of service is consistent with the clinical context: the provider must assess the acute complaint, consider the patient's active medication regimen including simvastatin, and determine whether the acute illness interacts with or complicates ongoing chronic disease management.
The payer's reliance on RARC N115, citing a Local Coverage Determination, does not render this service non-covered. LCDs govern coverage for specific procedures and diagnostic services; they do not categorically exclude medically necessary evaluation and management visits for acute illness in established patients. The assertion that documentation does not establish medical necessity is a conclusory statement that does not account for the clinical appropriateness of a physician visit for an acutely symptomatic established patient. MUSC Health requests that Absolute Total Care conduct a clinical review of the complete medical record for this encounter, including the physician's documentation of the presenting complaint, clinical assessment, and management plan, before upholding this denial.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that Absolute Total Care (Centene) overturn the denial of Claim MUSC-B898-3 and issue payment at the allowed amount of $378.21 in accordance with the contracted rate for CPT 99214 rendered on May 11, 2026. Should the plan require additional clinical documentation from the rendering provider, Dr. Robert K. Lindqvist, MUSC Health will facilitate prompt submission of the complete encounter record. This appeal is submitted within the 90-day dispute window, ahead of the September 8, 2026 deadline, through the secure provider portal as directed on the Explanation of Payment.

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health is submitting this formal first-level appeal on behalf of patient Mohamed Hermann (MRN: MUSC1465392, Member ID: CIG627241918, Group: GRP-90544) regarding the denial of Claim ID MUSC-BC1F-1, with a date of service of January 6, 2026, submitted on January 14, 2026. The claim was denied on February 13, 2026, under CARC 16 and RARC N290, with the payer remark stating: "Claim cannot be adjudicated; required data element(s) are missing or invalid," specifically citing a missing, incomplete, or invalid rendering provider primary identifier. MUSC Health respectfully disputes this denial and submits that the rendering provider's National Provider Identifier (NPI) was valid and present on the original claim submission.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Mr. Hermann, a 29-year-old established male patient, was seen on January 6, 2026, at MUSC Health University Medical Center in Charleston, SC, an on-campus outpatient hospital facility (Place of Service 22). The visit was rendered by Dr. Priya N. Raghavan, MD, and was billed under CPT code 99214, representing an office or outpatient visit for an established patient of moderate complexity, with a primary diagnosis of J06.9 (Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified) and a secondary diagnosis of R69. The claim was submitted with Revenue Code 0510 and reflects a billed amount of $694.01, against which Cigna's allowed amount was calculated at $490.24, with no payment issued.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The sole stated basis for denial is RARC N290, indicating that the rendering provider's primary identifier was missing, incomplete, or invalid. MUSC Health asserts that this characterization is inaccurate. Dr. Priya N. Raghavan, MD, holds an active and valid NPI of 1669504132, which was included on the claim as submitted on January 14, 2026. This NPI is registered in the National Plan and Provider Enumeration System (NPPES) and is the appropriate primary identifier for a rendering provider under HIPAA standard transaction requirements. If a data formatting or transmission issue caused the identifier to appear absent or unreadable during Cigna's adjudication process, that constitutes a technical processing error rather than a substantive deficiency in the claim. The underlying service was rendered by a credentialed, identifiable provider to a covered member during an active coverage period, and the claim contains all elements necessary for adjudication. Denial of payment on this basis, without providing an opportunity to correct a clerical or technical discrepancy, is inconsistent with standard claims processing obligations and applicable appeal rights under the plan.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that Cigna Healthcare reopen and reprocess Claim ID MUSC-BC1F-1 using the valid NPI on file for Dr. Priya N. Raghavan, MD (NPI 1669504132), and issue payment at the applicable contracted rate for CPT 99214 as rendered on January 6, 2026. Supporting documentation, including the medical record for the date of service and provider credentialing information confirming the active NPI, is enclosed with this appeal submission. Should Cigna require any additional information to complete adjudication, MUSC Health requests prompt written notification so that any outstanding items may be addressed without further delay. This appeal is being submitted within the applicable appeal deadline of August 12, 2026, through the designated portal in accordance with Cigna's appeal submission requirements.

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health is submitting this formal first-level appeal on behalf of patient Mohamed Hermann (MRN: MUSC1465392, Member ID: CIG627241918, Group: GRP-90544) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-BC1F-2 for services rendered on March 31, 2026, at MUSC Health University Medical Center. The claim was submitted on April 15, 2026, and denied on May 19, 2026, under CARC 204 ("This service/equipment/drug is not covered under the patient's current benefit plan") and RARC N130 ("Consult plan benefit documents/guidelines for information about restrictions for this service"), with the payer remark stating: "Service is excluded under the member's plan benefit document." MUSC Health respectfully disputes this determination and requests full reconsideration and payment of the billed amount of $415.38.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
On March 31, 2026, Dr. Sarah E. Whitmore, MD (NPI 1447382910) evaluated Mr. Hermann, a 29-year-old established male patient, in an on-campus outpatient hospital setting (Place of Service 22) for an acute upper respiratory infection (ICD-10 J06.9), with a secondary diagnosis of R69. The encounter was appropriately coded as CPT 99214, representing an office or outpatient visit for an established patient requiring moderate-complexity medical decision-making. One unit was billed under revenue code 0510 at a total charge of $415.38. Cigna Healthcare's own adjudication recognized an allowed amount of $257.84, which confirms the service falls within a recognized fee schedule and was not denied on the basis of coding error or lack of authorization.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial of this claim on benefit-exclusion grounds is not supported by the facts of this case. CPT 99214 is a standard evaluation and management service representing a medically necessary outpatient visit for an acute illness. Primary diagnosis: J06.9 — Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified
Denied amount: $400.66
Denial code: CARC 204 / RARC N130 — This service/equipment/drug is not covered under the patient's current benefit plan.
Appeal deadline: 2026-08-11

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health is submitting this first-level appeal on behalf of patient Mohamed Hermann (MRN: MUSC1465392, Member ID: CIG627241918, Group: GRP-90544) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-BC1F-3 for services rendered on December 22, 2025, at MUSC Health East Cooper Medical Center, Mount Pleasant, SC. Cigna Healthcare denied the claim in full on February 12, 2026, citing CARC 204 ("This service/equipment/drug is not covered under the patient's current benefit plan") and RARC N130 ("Consult plan benefit documents/guidelines for information about restrictions for this service"), with the payer remark stating the service is excluded under the member's plan benefit document. MUSC Health respectfully disputes this determination and requests a full reversal and payment at the allowed amount of $223.68.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
On December 22, 2025, Mr. Hermann, a 29-year-old established male patient, presented to MUSC Health East Cooper Medical Center for an outpatient evaluation and management visit rendered by Daniel R. Okafor, MD (NPI 1558493021). The encounter was billed under CPT code 99214, representing an office or outpatient visit for an established patient of moderate complexity, with a primary diagnosis of J06.9 (Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified) and a secondary diagnosis of R69. The claim was submitted on January 1, 2026, with a billed charge of $400.66. The service was provided in an on-campus outpatient hospital setting (Place of Service 22, Revenue Code 0510). Mr. Hermann's Cigna Healthcare Advantage plan carries a coverage period of January 1, 2024, through December 31, 2026, and was active at the time of service.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial of CPT 99214 as a non-covered benefit is not consistent with the nature of the service provided. CPT 99214 is a standard evaluation and management code representing a medically necessary outpatient visit for an established patient presenting with an acute condition. Evaluation and management services of this type are among the most fundamental components of outpatient medical care and are broadly covered under commercial health benefit plans. A blanket exclusion of a moderate-complexity established-patient office visit would be highly atypical under any comprehensive commercial plan, and Cigna has not provided specific contractual language or a benefit exclusion category sufficient to substantiate this denial.
MUSC Health requests that Cigna Healthcare identify with specificity the benefit exclusion provision under the Cigna Healthcare Advantage plan document that applies to this service. Without that specificity, the denial does not meet the standard of a reasoned coverage determination. Furthermore, the claim was submitted timely, the rendering provider is an enrolled participating provider under the applicable plan, the member's coverage was active on the date of service, and the diagnosis and procedure code are appropriately matched. There is no coding discrepancy, authorization issue, or coordination-of-benefits concern reflected in the denial record. The sole stated basis is a benefit exclusion, which MUSC Health contends has not been adequately supported.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that Cigna Healthcare conduct a complete review of this appeal, identify the specific plan exclusion language relied upon in issuing the denial, and reverse the denial in full. Upon reversal, MUSC Health requests that payment be issued at the contracted allowed amount of $223.68 in accordance with the terms of the participating provider agreement. Should Cigna uphold the denial, MUSC Health requests a written explanation citing the precise benefit document section and exclusion language applicable to CPT 99214 as billed on this claim, so that further appeal options may be evaluated. This appeal is submitted within the deadline of August 11, 2026, through the appropriate channel as directed in the denial notice.

RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Malik Ward (MRN MUSC6249242), Claim MUSC-C36D-1

Patient: Malik Ward  (DOB 1957-04-24)
MRN: MUSC6249242
Member ID / Group: UHC725804182 / GRP-83998
Claim number: MUSC-C36D-1
Date of service: 2025-08-18
Procedure billed: CPT 99214 — Office/outpatient visit, established patient, moderate complexity
Primary diagnosis: J06.9 — Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified
Denied amount: $392.73
Denial code: CARC 197 / RARC N54 — Precertification/authorization/notification/pre-treatment absent.
Appeal deadline: 2026-10-03

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health is submitting this formal first-level appeal on behalf of Malik Ward (Member ID: UHC725804182, Group: GRP-83998) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-C36D-1 for services rendered on August 18, 2025, by James H. Ferrell, MD (NPI 1992837465) at MUSC Health University Medical Center. The claim was denied under CARC 197 ("Precertification/authorization/notification/pre-treatment absent") and RARC N54 ("Claim information is inconsistent with pre-certified/authorized services"), with the payer remark stating "No prior authorization on file for the date of service billed." MUSC Health respectfully contends that this denial is inconsistent with the nature of the service provided and requests full reimbursement of the billed amount of $392.73.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Mr. Ward is a 69-year-old male with an established and complex medical history that includes active atrial fibrillation, managed continuously since May 2010, and obesity (BMI 30.55 kg/m²). His cardiac history is significant, encompassing multiple electrical cardioversions and catheter ablation procedures over the course of several years. He has been maintained on a long-standing medication regimen that includes Verapamil Hydrochloride, Warfarin Sodium, and Digoxin, all active since 2010, reflecting the ongoing and medically intensive nature of his cardiac management. On August 18, 2025, Mr. Ward presented to MUSC Health University Medical Center as an established outpatient patient and was evaluated by Dr. Ferrell. The encounter was billed as CPT 99214, an office or outpatient visit for an established patient of moderate complexity, with a primary diagnosis of acute upper respiratory infection (J06.9) and a secondary diagnosis of obesity (E66.9).

BASIS FOR APPEAL
CPT code 99214 represents a standard evaluation and management service for an established patient in an outpatient setting. Evaluation and management visits of this type, particularly for established patients presenting with acute conditions such as an upper respiratory infection, are widely recognized as routine outpatient services that do not require prior authorization under most commercial health plan benefit structures. UnitedHealthcare's denial rests solely on the assertion that no prior authorization was on file; however, MUSC Health's position is that no prior authorization was required for this category of service. An established-patient office visit billed under CPT 99214 is not a procedure, surgery, advanced imaging study, or other service type that customarily triggers a prior authorization requirement under standard commercial HMO plan designs.
Furthermore, Mr. Ward's active diagnoses — including atrial fibrillation requiring ongoing pharmacologic management with anticoagulation and rate-control agents — make periodic outpatient evaluation not only appropriate but medically necessary. The complexity of his medication regimen alone, which includes Warfarin Sodium and Digoxin, necessitates regular clinical oversight to ensure therapeutic safety and efficacy. The moderate complexity level assigned to this visit is consistent with the patient's documented comorbidities and the clinical judgment required to manage an acute illness in the context of his underlying conditions. The denial under RARC N54 further implies a discrepancy with pre-authorized services; however, if no authorization was sought because none was required, this remark code is inapplicable on its face.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that UnitedHealthcare conduct a thorough review of this appeal and confirm whether CPT 99214 rendered in an established outpatient setting is subject to prior authorization requirements under Mr. Ward's UnitedHealthcare HMO plan (Group: GRP-83998, coverage period January 1, 2024 through December 31, 2026). If prior authorization is not required for this service type, we request that the denial be reversed and that payment be issued at the contracted rate, with the allowed amount of $283.27 applied accordingly. Should UnitedHealthcare maintain that authorization was required, we request that the specific benefit provision or clinical policy mandating such authorization be provided in writing so that MUSC Health may respond with additional documentation. This appeal is submitted within the applicable appeal deadline of October 3, 2026, via the required electronic reconsideration process through the Claims and Payments portal.

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health is submitting this formal first-level appeal on behalf of Malik Ward (Member ID: UHC725804182, Group: GRP-83998, MRN: MUSC6249242, DOB: 1957-04-24) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-C36D-2 for services rendered on February 25, 2026, at MUSC Health Rutledge Tower Ambulatory Care. UnitedHealthcare denied the claim in full on April 21, 2026, citing CARC 197 ("Precertification/authorization/notification/pre-treatment absent") and RARC N54 ("Claim information is inconsistent with pre-certified/authorized services"), with the payer remark stating: "No prior authorization on file for the date of service billed." MUSC Health respectfully disputes this denial on the grounds that the service rendered — an established outpatient office visit for an acute upper respiratory condition — does not require prior authorization under applicable plan terms and standard commercial payer guidelines governing urgent, low-acuity ambulatory encounters.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Mr. Ward is a 69-year-old male with an active medical history that includes atrial fibrillation, managed long-term with Verapamil Hydrochloride, Digoxin, and Warfarin Sodium, as well as obesity (BMI 30.55 kg/m², ICD-10 E66.9). He presented on February 25, 2026, to Dr. Daniel R. Okafor, MD (NPI 1558493021) at MUSC Health Rutledge Tower Ambulatory Care, an on-campus outpatient hospital facility (Place of Service 22). The encounter was an established patient visit billed as CPT 99214, reflecting moderate medical decision-making, with a primary diagnosis of acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified (ICD-10 J06.9) and a secondary diagnosis of obesity (ICD-10 E66.9). The total billed amount was $403.49. Given Mr. Ward's underlying cardiac conditions and his anticoagulation regimen, clinical evaluation of an acute respiratory illness by his treating physician represents a medically appropriate and necessary service.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
Prior authorization requirements under commercial HMO plans are generally reserved for elective procedures, specialist referrals requiring gatekeeper approval, or high-cost diagnostic and surgical services. An established patient office visit for evaluation and management of an acute upper respiratory infection is a routine, time-sensitive ambulatory service for which imposing a prior authorization requirement would be both clinically impractical and inconsistent with broadly accepted managed care standards. Acute illnesses, by their nature, do not afford patients or providers the opportunity to seek prospective authorization before care is delivered. Requiring prior authorization for such encounters would create barriers to medically necessary care and is not consistent with the intent of utilization management programs.
Furthermore, CPT 99214 is a standard evaluation and management code for established outpatient patients presenting with moderate complexity. The service was rendered by a credentialed provider at a contracted MUSC Health facility during an active coverage period (January 1, 2024, through December 31, 2026). No clinical or coding irregularity has been identified that would independently support denial. The payer's own remittance reflects an allowed amount of $256.25, which indicates the service itself is a covered benefit — the sole stated basis for non-payment is the absence of prior authorization. MUSC Health respectfully asserts that prior authorization was not required for this category of service and that the denial therefore lacks a valid contractual or clinical basis.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health requests that UnitedHealthcare conduct a full reconsideration of Claim MUSC-C36D-2 and issue payment at the previously established allowed amount of $256.25, consistent with the applicable contractual rate for CPT 99214 rendered at Place of Service 22. Should the plan maintain that prior authorization was required for this encounter, MUSC Health further requests that UnitedHealthcare provide, in writing, the specific plan provision or utilization management policy that mandates precertification for established patient evaluation and management visits for acute illness, so that any administrative process gap may be addressed prospectively. This appeal is submitted within the plan's stated 365-day filing window and via the required electronic reconsideration channel.

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health is submitting this formal appeal on behalf of Malik Ward (Member ID: UHC725804182, Group: GRP-83998) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-C36D-3, covering services rendered on January 25, 2026, by Elena V. DEN-MUSC-CC97-1.letter_text:
RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Jenee Turcotte (MRN MUSC0686121), Claim MUSC-CC97-1

Patient: Jenee Turcotte  (DOB 1979-12-30)
MRN: MUSC0686121

Claim number: MUSC-CC97-1
Date of service: 2026-03-02
Procedure billed: CPT 99214 — Office/outpatient visit, established patient, moderate complexity
Primary diagnosis: E66.9 — Obesity, unspecified
Denied amount: $492.45
Denial code: CARC 50 / RARC N115 — These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
Appeal deadline: 2027-03-20

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health is submitting this formal first-level appeal on behalf of patient Jenee Turcotte (MRN: MUSC0686121, Member ID: UHC683527916, Group: GRP-16096) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-CC97-1 for services rendered on March 2, 2026, at MUSC Health Florence Medical Center. UnitedHealthcare denied the claim under CARC 50 ("These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer") and RARC N115 ("This decision was based on a Local Coverage Determination (LCD)"), with the accompanying remark that "Documentation submitted does not establish that the service was reasonable and necessary for the diagnosis reported." MUSC Health respectfully disagrees with this determination and requests full reversal and payment at the allowed amount of $307.21.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Ms. Turcotte is a 46-year-old female with an established, active diagnosis of obesity (E66.9), documented as ongoing since May 2015, and a longstanding history of hypertension (I10), active since 1998 and currently managed with hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg. She presented on March 2, 2026, as an established outpatient patient to Dr. Elena V. Castellanos, MD (NPI 1881726354) at MUSC Health Florence Medical Center, an on-campus outpatient hospital facility (Place of Service 22). The visit was billed as CPT 99214, an office or outpatient visit for an established patient requiring moderate-complexity medical decision-making, with a primary diagnosis of E66.9 and a secondary diagnosis of J06.9.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial of this claim as not medically necessary is not supported by the clinical facts of record. Obesity (E66.9) is a chronic, progressive disease with well-established associations with serious comorbid conditions. Ms. Turcotte carries an active diagnosis of hypertension managed with ongoing pharmacotherapy, a condition directly compounded by obesity. The co-occurrence of these two active, chronic conditions in a 46-year-old patient creates a clinical picture that unambiguously warrants regular physician evaluation and management. A level-4 established patient visit (CPT 99214) is consistent with the moderate complexity inherent in managing a patient with multiple active chronic conditions requiring ongoing assessment, medication management, and risk stratification.
The selection of CPT 99214 is appropriate under current Evaluation and Management coding guidelines, which base level selection on medical decision-making complexity or total time. Managing two interrelated chronic conditions — obesity and hypertension — in a single encounter supports a moderate-complexity determination. The claim was submitted correctly with supporting diagnoses, and the rendering provider's documentation should reflect the clinical rationale for the visit level selected. If UnitedHealthcare's review was conducted without access to the complete encounter documentation, MUSC Health respectfully requests that a clinical reviewer re-evaluate the record in its entirety prior to issuing a final determination.
Furthermore, to the extent this denial relies on a Local Coverage Determination, MUSC Health notes that LCDs govern Medicare coverage policy and are not directly applicable to commercial PPO claims. Applying an LCD framework to a commercially insured member's claim without a corresponding contractual basis would be inconsistent with the terms of the parties' agreement and with generally accepted standards for commercial claims adjudication.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that UnitedHealthcare conduct a full clinical review of this appeal, including all submitted encounter documentation, and reverse the denial of Claim MUSC-CC97-1. We request that payment be issued at the contractually allowed amount of $307.21 for CPT 99214 rendered on March 2, 2026. Should UnitedHealthcare require additional clinical documentation to support this appeal, please contact MUSC Health's Revenue Cycle Appeals team promptly so that records may be provided within the applicable timeframe. We ask that this appeal be resolved in accordance with UnitedHealthcare's prompt-pay and appeal-response obligations under applicable state and federal requirements.

Whitmore, MD. The claim was denied on April 5, 2026 under CARC 16 / RARC N290, with the payer remark stating: "Claim cannot be adjudicated; required data element(s) are missing or invalid," specifically citing a missing, incomplete, or invalid rendering provider primary identifier. MUSC Health respectfully disputes this denial and asserts that the rendering provider's National Provider Identifier (NPI) was valid and present on the original claim submission.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Ms. Turcotte is a 46-year-old established female patient with active diagnoses of obesity (E66.9, onset 2015) and hypertension (I10, onset 1998), for which she carries an ongoing prescription for Hydrochlorothiazide 25 MG. She presented on March 5, 2026 at MUSC Health Florence Medical Center (Place of Service 22, On Campus Outpatient Hospital) for an outpatient evaluation and management visit of moderate complexity, billed under CPT 99214. The visit was rendered by Sarah E. Whitmore, MD, whose NPI on file with MUSC Health is 1447382910. The claim was submitted on March 9, 2026, within four days of the date of service, with a billed amount of $594.59.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The sole stated basis for denial is RARC N290 — missing, incomplete, or invalid rendering provider primary identifier. MUSC Health has verified that NPI 1447382910 for Dr. Sarah E. Whitmore was included in the original claim submission in the appropriate data field. This NPI is an active, Type 1 individual provider identifier consistent with CMS requirements for outpatient professional billing. The denial does not appear to reflect an actual absence of this data element, but rather a potential processing or system matching error on the part of UnitedHealthcare during adjudication.
CPT 99214 was appropriately reported for an established patient office visit of moderate complexity, consistent with the patient's active chronic conditions requiring ongoing management. The primary diagnosis of E66.9 (obesity, unspecified) accurately reflects the documented, active condition with onset in 2015, and the secondary diagnosis of J06.9 was submitted as coded in the patient's medical record. The claim was submitted timely, the member's coverage period runs through December 31, 2026, and no clinical or coverage-based denial reason has been cited by UnitedHealthcare. The denial is purely administrative in nature and does not reflect any question of medical necessity or benefit eligibility.
MUSC Health requests that UnitedHealthcare re-examine the original claim transaction to confirm that NPI 1447382910 was transmitted in the correct loop and segment per standard HIPAA 837P transaction requirements. If a technical transmission discrepancy is identified, we are prepared to resubmit a corrected claim immediately upon notification of the specific deficiency. However, based on our internal review, the NPI was present and valid as submitted.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that UnitedHealthcare reverse the denial of Claim ID MUSC-CC97-2 and reprocess the claim for payment at the contracted allowed amount of $277.18. Should UnitedHealthcare identify a specific and correctable data element deficiency upon review of the original transaction, we request prompt written notification so that a corrected submission may be made without delay. This appeal is submitted in advance of the appeal deadline of April 5, 2027, via the required electronic reconsideration process through the Claims & Payments portal.

MUSC Health respectfully disagrees with this determination and requests full reversal and payment at the allowed amount of $253.66.

Ms. Turcotte is a 46-year-old female established patient with a documented, active diagnosis of obesity (ICD-10 E66.9), with onset recorded as May 4, 2015, and a confirmed body mass index of 30.33 kg/m² on file. She additionally carries an active diagnosis of hypertension (ICD-10 I10), with onset dating to August 10, 1998, and is currently maintained on Hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg. BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial of CPT 99214 for an established patient visit addressing active obesity is not supported by the clinical record. Obesity (E66.9) is a recognized, chronic, and progressive disease with well-established associations with cardiovascular risk, including hypertension, which Ms. Turcotte has been managing pharmacologically for nearly three decades. MUSC Health maintains that the documentation supports the medical necessity of this service and that the denial does not reflect a complete review of the clinical record.

Should the reviewer require additional clinical documentation from the treating provider, Dr. Raghavan, or from the medical record, MUSC Health will cooperate promptly to facilitate that review. If this first-level appeal is not resolved in favor of the patient, we reserve all rights to pursue subsequent levels of appeal, including external independent review, in accordance with applicable state and federal requirements.

His active conditions include atrial fibrillation, for which he has carried a chronic medication regimen of Digoxin, Verapamil Hydrochloride, and Warfarin Sodium since 1994, and has undergone multiple electrical cardioversions and cardiac catheter ablation procedures over the years. Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health Florence Medical Center submits this formal reconsideration request on behalf of patient Jerrell Gerlach (MRN: MUSC3906137, Member ID: BCB447669083, Group: GRP-66199) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-D48A-2 for services rendered on June 16, 2026. The claim was denied on August 8, 2026, under CARC 16 / RARC N290, with the payer remark stating: "Claim cannot be adjudicated; required data element(s) are missing or invalid," citing a missing, incomplete, or invalid rendering provider primary identifier. MUSC Health respectfully disputes this denial and submits that the rendering provider's National Provider Identifier (NPI) was valid and on file at the time of submission. We request full adjudication and payment of this claim.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Mr. Gerlach is an 87-year-old male with an established and complex medical history managed at MUSC Health Florence Medical Center. His active conditions include anemia (D64.9), atrial fibrillation, carcinoma in situ of the prostate, and prediabetes, and he carries a long-standing medication regimen that includes Warfarin Sodium, Digoxin, Verapamil Hydrochloride, Leuprolide Acetate, and DOCEtaxel. On June 16, 2026, Mr. Gerlach was seen as an established outpatient by Robert K. Lindqvist, MD (NPI 1314059687) at MUSC Health Florence Medical Center, Place of Service 22. The encounter was billed as CPT 99214, an office or outpatient visit for an established patient of moderate complexity, with a primary diagnosis of acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified (J06.9), and a secondary diagnosis of anemia (D64.9). The total billed amount was $537.47, against a payer-allowed amount of $305.55. No payment was issued.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The sole stated basis for denial is RARC N290, indicating that the rendering provider's primary identifier — the NPI — was missing, incomplete, or invalid on the submitted claim. MUSC Health asserts that this characterization is inaccurate. Robert K. Lindqvist, MD holds NPI 1314059687, which is an active, valid Type 1 NPI registered in the National Plan and Provider Enumeration System (NPPES). This NPI was included on the original claim submission dated July 1, 2026. A billing error of this nature, if any discrepancy exists, constitutes a correctable administrative deficiency and does not reflect any question of medical necessity, coverage eligibility, or coding accuracy. CPT 99214 is an appropriate level of service for an established patient visit of moderate complexity given Mr. Gerlach's active, multifaceted conditions and ongoing medication management. The patient's coverage under BlueCross BlueShield of South Carolina Choice Plus was active on the date of service, with a coverage period extending through December 31, 2026. There is no clinical, contractual, or coding basis to deny payment for this encounter.
We are submitting this appeal through the My Insurance Manager (MIM) portal in accordance with the instructions provided on the remittance advice, and we are attaching the relevant remittance advice and supporting medical record documentation as directed.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that BlueCross BlueShield of South Carolina reprocess Claim MUSC-D48A-2 in full, recognizing NPI 1314059687 as a valid and active rendering provider identifier for Robert K. Lindqvist, MD, and issue payment at the allowed amount of $305.55 in accordance with the terms of the BlueCross BlueShield of South Carolina Choice Plus plan. Should any additional documentation or corrected claim submission be required to resolve this administrative matter, we ask that the payer contact MUSC Health Revenue Cycle directly so that any outstanding requirement may be addressed promptly and without further delay to adjudication.

DEN-MUSC-D48A-3.letter_text:
RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Jerrell Gerlach (MRN MUSC3906137), Claim MUSC-D48A-3

Patient: Jerrell Gerlach  (DOB 1939-01-27)
MRN: MUSC3906137
Member ID / Group: BCB447669083 / GRP-66199
Claim number: MUSC-D48A-3
Date of service: 2026-04-15
Procedure billed: CPT 93458 — Left heart catheterization with coronary angiography
Primary diagnosis: J06.9 — Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified
Denied amount: $9,578.14
Denial code: CARC 50 / RARC N115 — These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
Appeal deadline: 2026-09-01

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health is submitting this formal first-level reconsideration on behalf of patient Jerrell Gerlach (MRN: MUSC3906137, Member ID: BCB447669083, Group: GRP-66199) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-D48A-3 for services rendered on April 15, 2026, at MUSC Health University Medical Center. BlueCross BlueShield of South Carolina denied the claim under CARC 50 ("These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer") with RARC N115, citing a Local Coverage Determination, and further noted that "documentation submitted does not establish that the service was reasonable and necessary for the diagnosis reported." MUSC Health respectfully disagrees with this determination and submits that the denial is the result of a coding discrepancy that, when corrected, fully supports the medical necessity of the procedure performed.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Mr. Gerlach is an 87-year-old male with a complex and longstanding cardiac history. He has carried a diagnosis of atrial fibrillation since 1994 and has been continuously managed with Verapamil Hydrochloride, Digoxin, and Warfarin Sodium since that time — a regimen consistent with rate control and anticoagulation therapy for chronic atrial fibrillation. His cardiac history is further documented by multiple electrical cardioversions performed in 2018, 2019, and 2020, as well as catheter ablations of cardiac tissue performed in 2017 and 2018, reflecting a pattern of recurrent, refractory atrial fibrillation requiring escalating intervention over many years. He also carries active diagnoses of anemia (D64.9) and prostate neoplasm, and is currently receiving Docetaxel and Leuprolide Acetate, agents associated with known cardiovascular effects. This clinical profile — a geriatric patient with decades of atrial fibrillation, prior ablations, prior cardioversions, active oncologic therapy, and anticoagulation — represents precisely the population for whom left heart catheterization with coronary angiography (CPT 93458) is a recognized and medically necessary diagnostic tool.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The payer's denial rests on the assertion that the submitted documentation does not support medical necessity for the diagnosis reported. MUSC Health acknowledges that the primary diagnosis code submitted on this claim — J06.9, Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified — does not reflect the clinical indication that prompted CPT 93458 on April 15, 2026. This represents a coding error on the submitted claim, not an absence of medical necessity. The correct primary diagnosis should reflect Mr. Gerlach's active, chronic atrial fibrillation and his broader cardiovascular condition, which are thoroughly documented in his longitudinal medical record. The secondary diagnosis of D64.9 (Anemia) was correctly reported and is clinically relevant given his active oncologic treatment. A corrected claim with the appropriate primary diagnosis code will be submitted concurrently with this appeal. We respectfully request that BlueCross BlueShield of South Carolina evaluate this appeal in conjunction with the corrected claim and the accompanying medical records, which clearly establish the cardiac indication for the procedure. The procedure was performed by Daniel R. Okafor, MD (NPI 1558493021) in an on-campus outpatient hospital setting, consistent with the acuity and complexity of Mr. Gerlach's condition.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health requests that BlueCross BlueShield of South Carolina overturn the denial of Claim MUSC-D48A-3 and reprocess the claim for payment upon receipt of the corrected claim reflecting the appropriate primary diagnosis. The billed amount for CPT 93458 is $9,578.14, with a payer-allowed amount of $6,750.78 on file. We ask that the claim be adjudicated at the contracted allowed amount in accordance with the terms of the BlueCross BlueShield of South Carolina Choice Plus plan. All supporting medical records documenting Mr. Gerlach's cardiac history and the clinical indication for this procedure are attached for review. This reconsideration is being submitted through My Insurance Manager (MIM) in advance of the appeal deadline of September 1, 2026, as required.

DEN-MUSC-D48A-4.argument_summary: Denial based on a mismatched primary diagnosis code should be reversed; the full cardiac record establishes medical necessity for CPT 93458 in this patient with refractory atrial fibrillation.
DEN-MUSC-D48A-4.letter_text:
RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Jerrell Gerlach (MRN MUSC3906137), Claim MUSC-D48A-4

Patient: Jerrell Gerlach  (DOB 1939-01-27)
MRN: MUSC3906137
Member ID / Group: BCB447669083 / GRP-66199
Claim number: MUSC-D48A-4
Date of service: 2026-05-17
Procedure billed: CPT 93458 — Left heart catheterization with coronary angiography
Primary diagnosis: J06.9 — Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified
Denied amount: $12,559.35
Denial code: CARC 50 / RARC N115 — These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
Appeal deadline: 2026-10-05

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health respectfully submits this first-level provider reconsideration on behalf of patient Jerrell Gerlach (MRN: MUSC3906137, Member ID: BCB447669083, Group: GRP-66199) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-D48A-4 for services rendered on May 17, 2026, at MUSC Health Rutledge Tower Ambulatory Care. BlueCross BlueShield of South Carolina denied the claim under CARC 50 ("These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer") with RARC N115, citing a Local Coverage Determination, and remarked that "documentation submitted does not establish that the service was reasonable and necessary for the diagnosis reported." We respectfully disagree and request full reversal and payment at the allowed amount of $8,701.66.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Mr. Gerlach is an 87-year-old male with a longstanding and clinically complex cardiac history. He carries an active diagnosis of atrial fibrillation with onset dating to May 1994, managed continuously with Verapamil Hydrochloride, Digoxin, and Warfarin Sodium — a regimen in place for over three decades. His cardiac history includes multiple electrical cardioversions (July 2018, November 2019, November 2020) and two catheter ablations of cardiac tissue (July 2017, November 2018), reflecting a pattern of recurrent, refractory atrial fibrillation requiring escalating intervention. Concurrent active conditions include anemia (D64.9), prostate neoplasm under active treatment with Docetaxel and Leuprolide Acetate, and prediabetes. His former smoking status and lipid profile further contribute to his overall cardiovascular risk burden.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The payer's denial appears to rest entirely on the primary diagnosis code submitted — J06.9 (Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified) — which, standing alone, would not ordinarily support left heart catheterization with coronary angiography (CPT 93458). We acknowledge this coding discrepancy and submit that it does not accurately reflect the clinical indication for the procedure. The secondary diagnosis of D64.9 (Anemia, unspecified) was submitted alongside the claim, and the complete medical record documents active, long-standing atrial fibrillation as the patient's dominant cardiac condition. The presence of J06.9 as the primary billed diagnosis appears to be a coding error that does not reflect the treating physician's documented clinical rationale.
Dr. Elena V. Castellanos, MD (NPI 1881726354), performed CPT 93458 in the context of a patient with decades of atrial fibrillation, multiple failed cardioversions, prior catheter ablations, and ongoing antiarrhythmic and anticoagulation therapy. In an 87-year-old patient with this history, coronary angiography in conjunction with left heart catheterization is consistent with generally accepted standards of care for evaluating coronary anatomy prior to further electrophysiologic or structural intervention, or for assessing ischemic contributors to arrhythmia burden. The medical necessity of this procedure is supported by the totality of the patient's documented cardiac history, not by the primary diagnosis code alone.
We are submitting the complete encounter documentation, the remittance advice for Claim MUSC-D48A-4, and the relevant portions of Mr. Gerlach's longitudinal cardiac record in accordance with BlueCross BlueShield of South Carolina's reconsideration requirements through the My Insurance Manager portal. We respectfully request that the clinical reviewer evaluate medical necessity based on the full clinical record rather than the face of the submitted diagnosis code.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health requests that BlueCross BlueShield of South Carolina overturn the medical necessity denial for Claim MUSC-D48A-4, CPT 93458, date of service May 17, 2026, and reprocess the claim for payment at the previously established allowed amount of $8,701.66. Should the reviewer determine that a coding correction is required to align the primary diagnosis with the documented clinical indication, we further request that the claim be reopened for resubmission with corrected diagnosis coding rather than adjudicated as a final denial. This reconsideration is submitted in advance of the appeal deadline of October 5, 2026.

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health submits this first-level redetermination request to Palmetto GBA on behalf of patient Tom Goodwin (MRN: MUSC6218426, Member ID: MED793863465) regarding Claim ID MUSC-DA2C-1, covering a date of service of June 20, 2026. The claim was submitted on June 27, 2026, and was denied on August 3, 2026, with CARC 197 (Precertification/authorization/notification/pre-treatment absent) and RARC N54 (Claim information is inconsistent with pre-certified/authorized services), accompanied by the payer remark: "No prior authorization on file for the date of service billed." This appeal is submitted within the 120-day redetermination filing window, ahead of the December 1, 2026 deadline.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Mr. Goodwin is a 58-year-old male with an established and active history of hyperlipidemia (E78.5, onset May 2020), obesity (E66.9, onset May 2012), prediabetes, and anemia. He has been an established patient in the MUSC Health system with documented longitudinal care, including prior medication reconciliation, review of systems, and laboratory monitoring. He is currently maintained on Simvastatin 10 mg, ordered June 2, 2020, for management of his hyperlipidemia. The June 20, 2026 encounter, billed as CPT 99214, was a follow-up outpatient visit rendered by Dr. James H. Ferrell, MD (NPI 1992837465) at MUSC Health Ashley River Tower, an on-campus outpatient hospital facility (Place of Service 22). The visit addressed his active, chronic conditions, consistent with the established-patient moderate-complexity evaluation and management service billed.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial on the basis of absent prior authorization is not applicable to this claim under Medicare Fee-for-Service rules. Medicare FFS — administered in this jurisdiction by Palmetto GBA as the JM MAC — does not require prior authorization for outpatient evaluation and management services such as CPT 99214 rendered in a physician office or outpatient hospital setting for the management of established chronic conditions. CPT 99214 appropriately reflects a moderate-complexity established-patient visit involving review and management of these conditions. The billed amount of $533.62, with an allowed amount of $391.18 already calculated by the payer, further confirms that the service was recognized as a covered benefit; the sole stated basis for zero payment is the prior authorization issue, which does not apply here.

MUSC Health respectfully requests that Palmetto GBA reverse the denial of Claim MUSC-DA2C-1 and reprocess the claim for payment at the allowed amount of $391.18, in accordance with Medicare FFS coverage rules and correct coding guidelines applicable to outpatient evaluation and management services. Should additional documentation — including the medical record for the June 20, 2026 encounter or supporting clinical notes — be required to complete this redetermination, MUSC Health will provide those materials promptly upon request.

DEN-MUSC-E622-1.argument_summary: A chest X-ray rendered in a hospital emergency room is exempt from prior authorization under federal Medicaid MCO rules; denial solely for absent precertification is legally unsupportable.
DEN-MUSC-E622-1.letter_text:
RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Lonnie Von (MRN MUSC3090378), Claim MUSC-E622-1

Patient: Lonnie Von  (DOB 1950-08-03)
MRN: MUSC3090378
Member ID / Group: MOL918865725 / GRP-17484
Claim number: MUSC-E622-1
Date of service: 2026-04-09
Procedure billed: CPT 71046 — Radiologic examination, chest; 2 views
Primary diagnosis: S72.001A — Fracture of unspecified part of neck of femur, initial encounter
Denied amount: $279.27
Denial code: CARC 197 / RARC N54 — Precertification/authorization/notification/pre-treatment absent.
Appeal deadline: 2026-08-11

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health Florence Medical Center submits this formal appeal on behalf of patient Lonnie Von (MRN: MUSC3090378, Member ID: MOL918865725) regarding the denial of Claim ID MUSC-E622-1 for services rendered on April 9, 2026, at the emergency room of MUSC Health Florence Medical Center. The claim was submitted on April 24, 2026, and denied on May 13, 2026, with CARC 197 ("Precertification/authorization/notification/pre-treatment absent") and RARC N54 ("Claim information is inconsistent with pre-certified/authorized services"), accompanied by the payer remark: "No prior authorization on file for the date of service billed." MUSC Health respectfully disputes this denial. The service at issue — a two-view chest radiograph (CPT 71046) performed in a hospital emergency room (Place of Service 23) — is an emergent diagnostic service for which prior authorization requirements are inapplicable under both federal Medicaid managed care regulations and Molina Healthcare of South Carolina's own obligations as a Medicaid managed care organization.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Mr. Von is a 76-year-old male with an active history of osteoporosis and a pathological fracture of the femoral neck (ICD-10 S72.001A), for which he has been maintained on alendronic acid since 2011. He presented to the MUSC Health Florence Medical Center emergency room on April 9, 2026. The encounter was classified as an emergency room admission. The primary diagnosis recorded for this visit is fracture of unspecified part of neck of femur, initial encounter (S72.001A), with a secondary diagnosis of J06.9. Rendering provider Daniel R. Okafor, MD (NPI 1558493021) ordered a two-view radiologic examination of the chest (CPT 71046, Revenue Code 0450), billed at $279.27. The total amount denied is $279.27, with an allowed amount of $174.63 on file, indicating the payer has already established a contractual rate for this service.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
Federal regulations governing Medicaid managed care organizations, codified at 42 C.F.R. § 438.114, explicitly prohibit a Medicaid MCO from requiring prior authorization for emergency services. An emergency department encounter by definition involves a presentation in which a prudent layperson could reasonably expect that the absence of immediate medical attention could result in serious jeopardy to health. A 76-year-old patient with documented osteoporosis and an active femoral neck fracture presenting to an emergency room represents precisely such a circumstance. The chest radiograph performed during this encounter is a standard, clinically indicated diagnostic study obtained in the course of emergency evaluation and management. It is not a scheduled, elective procedure for which advance notice to the payer is feasible or required.
The payer's own denial language — "No prior authorization on file for the date of service billed" — confirms that the denial rests solely on the absence of precertification. Because the service was rendered in an emergency room setting (Place of Service 23), no prior authorization was obtainable or required. The fact that Molina has already calculated an allowed amount of $174.63 for this claim further demonstrates that the service is a covered benefit under the Molina Healthcare of South Carolina Choice Plus plan (Coverage period: 2024-01-01 to 2026-12-31); the sole stated basis for non-payment is the prior authorization requirement, which cannot lawfully be applied to emergency services. Denial of payment on this basis is therefore inconsistent with applicable Medicaid managed care standards and with the terms of coverage in effect on the date of service.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that Molina Healthcare of South Carolina overturn the denial of Claim ID MUSC-E622-1, waive the prior authorization requirement as inapplicable to emergency room services, and reprocess the claim for payment at the contracted allowed amount of $174.63. Should Molina require additional clinical documentation, operative notes, or records from the April 9, 2026 encounter to complete its review, MUSC Health will provide those materials promptly upon request. We ask that this appeal be resolved within the timeframe required under applicable Medicaid managed care appeal regulations and the terms of our provider agreement.

RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Lonnie Von (MRN MUSC3090378), Claim MUSC-E622-2

Patient: Lonnie Von  (DOB 1950-08-03)
