Denial code: CARC 96 / RARC N130 — Non-covered charge(s).
Appeal deadline: 2026-09-11

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health respectfully submits this first-level provider appeal on behalf of patient Lonnie Von (Member ID: MOL918865725, MRN: MUSC3090378, Date of Birth: August 3, 1950) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-E622-2 for services rendered on April 22, 2026, at MUSC Health Ashley River Tower. Molina Healthcare of South Carolina denied the claim in full, citing CARC 96 ("Non-covered charge(s)") and RARC N130 ("Consult plan benefit documents/guidelines for information about restrictions for this service"), with the payer remark stating: "Service is excluded under the member's plan benefit document." The billed amount of $528.15 for one unit of CPT 99214 remains unpaid. MUSC Health contends that this denial is not supported by the clinical facts of the encounter and respectfully requests that Molina Healthcare reverse the denial and remit payment at the allowed amount of $395.08.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Mr. Von is a 76-year-old male enrolled in the Molina Healthcare of South Carolina Choice Plus plan (Group GRP-17484) with a coverage period extending through December 31, 2026. He carries an active diagnosis of pathological fracture due to osteoporosis, coded as S72.001A (fracture of unspecified part of neck of femur, initial encounter), with onset documented as February 12, 2021. His medical history is significant for osteoporosis, history of cardiac arrest, and a prior fracture of the forearm. He is currently maintained on alendronic acid 10 mg for osteoporosis management, as well as acetaminophen/hydrocodone and naproxen sodium for pain, all of which were ordered in connection with his fracture-related care. The April 22, 2026, encounter was performed by Amara J. Boone, NP (NPI 1203948576) in an on-campus outpatient hospital setting (Place of Service 22) and was billed under revenue code 0510. The visit was coded at the 99214 level, reflecting an established patient office visit of moderate complexity, which is consistent with the ongoing management of an active pathological fracture in an elderly patient with multiple comorbidities.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial of CPT 99214 as a "non-covered" service is inconsistent with the scope of benefits that South Carolina Medicaid managed care organizations are required to provide to enrolled beneficiaries. Outpatient evaluation and management services for established patients are a standard, covered benefit under Medicaid managed care contracts, and MUSC Health is not aware of any plan exclusion that would categorically remove medically necessary outpatient E/M visits from coverage. Molina's citation of RARC N130 directs the provider to consult plan benefit documents, yet no specific exclusion language has been communicated to support this denial. The service was rendered by a licensed nurse practitioner operating within an enrolled, credentialed facility, and the diagnosis of an active pathological femoral neck fracture in a 76-year-old patient on ongoing pharmacologic therapy clearly establishes medical necessity for continued outpatient follow-up. The level of service billed, 99214, is appropriate given the complexity of managing an active fracture with osteoporosis, a history of cardiac arrest, and a multi-drug medication regimen requiring monitoring. No coding error, duplicate claim, or eligibility issue has been cited by the payer as a basis for denial.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that Molina Healthcare of South Carolina conduct a full review of this appeal, reverse the denial of Claim MUSC-E622-2, and issue payment at the previously determined allowed amount of $395.08 for CPT 99214 rendered on April 22, 2026. Should Molina require additional clinical documentation, operative notes, or provider attestation to support this appeal, MUSC Health will promptly supply any requested materials. We ask that this matter be resolved within the timeframes required under applicable state Medicaid managed care appeal regulations.

DEN-MUSC-E622-3.argument_summary: A 76-year-old with documented osteoporosis and prior colonoscopies received medically warranted surveillance; the diagnosis-procedure mismatch is a correctable coding issue, not a medical necessity failure.
DEN-MUSC-E622-3.letter_text:
RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Lonnie Von (MRN MUSC3090378), Claim MUSC-E622-3

Patient: Lonnie Von  (DOB 1950-08-03)
MRN: MUSC3090378
Member ID / Group: MOL918865725 / GRP-17484
Claim number: MUSC-E622-3
Date of service: 2026-04-19
Procedure billed: CPT 45378 — Colonoscopy, flexible; diagnostic
Primary diagnosis: S72.001A — Fracture of unspecified part of neck of femur, initial encounter
Denied amount: $5,996.94
Denial code: CARC 50 / RARC N115 — These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
Appeal deadline: 2026-08-20

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health submits this first-level appeal on behalf of patient Lonnie Von (MRN: MUSC3090378, Member ID: MOL918865725) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-E622-3 for services rendered on April 19, 2026, at MUSC Health Rutledge Tower Ambulatory Care. Molina Healthcare of South Carolina denied the claim under CARC 50 ("These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer") and RARC N115 ("This decision was based on a Local Coverage Determination (LCD)"), with the accompanying remark that "Documentation submitted does not establish that the service was reasonable and necessary for the diagnosis reported." MUSC Health respectfully disagrees with this determination and requests a full reconsideration and reversal of the denial.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Mr. Von is a 76-year-old male with a documented history of osteoporosis, active since 2011, for which he has been maintained on alendronic acid 10 mg oral tablet since March 2011. He sustained a pathological fracture associated with his osteoporosis, with an onset recorded in February 2021, and has been managed with acetaminophen/hydrocodone bitartrate and naproxen sodium since that time. His medical history is further notable for a history of cardiac arrest, adding to the complexity of his overall clinical profile. The colonoscopy performed by Dr. Priya N. Raghavan (NPI 1669504132) on April 19, 2026, was billed under CPT 45378 at an on-campus outpatient hospital setting (Place of Service 22). The patient's prior procedure history includes a colonoscopy performed in July 2020 and an earlier colonoscopy in July 2015, establishing a pattern of ongoing colorectal surveillance in this elderly patient.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The payer's denial rests on the assertion that the submitted documentation does not establish medical necessity for the diagnosis reported. MUSC Health acknowledges that the primary diagnosis code submitted on the claim, S72.001A (fracture of unspecified part of neck of femur, initial encounter), does not on its face reflect a colorectal indication. However, this does not negate the clinical necessity of the colonoscopy itself. Mr. Von is a 76-year-old male with multiple active comorbidities, including long-standing osteoporosis and a history of cardiac arrest, and has an established history of periodic colonoscopic surveillance as evidenced by procedures performed in 2015 and 2020. The interval between the 2020 and 2026 procedures is consistent with surveillance intervals recognized under generally accepted gastroenterological standards for patients of his age and risk profile.
To the extent the denial was influenced by a perceived mismatch between the procedure and the reported diagnosis codes, MUSC Health is prepared to submit supplemental documentation from the treating provider, Dr. Raghavan, clarifying the clinical indication for the procedure. A coding discrepancy, if present, does not constitute a basis for a medical necessity denial; it is a correctable billing matter that should be addressed through a request for additional documentation rather than an outright denial with zero payment against a billed amount of $5,996.94. MUSC Health further notes that Molina's own allowed amount of $3,243.50 was calculated on this claim, suggesting the service itself falls within covered benefits, making the full denial to $0.00 paid inconsistent with that contractual determination.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that Molina Healthcare of South Carolina overturn the medical necessity denial for Claim MUSC-E622-3 and reprocess the claim for payment at the applicable contracted rate. If Molina requires additional clinical documentation, operative notes, or a letter of medical necessity from Dr. Raghavan to support this appeal, MUSC Health will provide those records promptly upon request. This appeal is submitted within the 90-day appeal window, prior to the stated deadline of August 20, 2026, and MUSC Health expects a written determination in accordance with Molina's appeal response obligations under South Carolina Medicaid managed care regulations.

DEN-MUSC-F1C0-1.argument_summary: One unit of CPT 99214 billed once for one date of service cannot exceed frequency limits; the denial is factually unsupported and should be reversed.
DEN-MUSC-F1C0-1.letter_text:
RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Kristie Effertz (MRN MUSC2132487), Claim MUSC-F1C0-1

Patient: Kristie Effertz  (DOB 1945-03-23)
MRN: MUSC2132487
Member ID / Group: CIG607831767 / GRP-43365
Claim number: MUSC-F1C0-1
Date of service: 2026-04-18
Procedure billed: CPT 99214 — Office/outpatient visit, established patient, moderate complexity
Primary diagnosis: J06.9 — Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified
Denied amount: $386.39
Denial code: CARC 151 / RARC N362 — Payer deems the information submitted does not support this many/frequency of services.
Appeal deadline: 2026-11-14

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health Florence Medical Center submits this formal first-level appeal on behalf of patient Kristie Effertz (MRN: MUSC2132487, Member ID: CIG607831767, Group: GRP-43365) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-F1C0-1 for services rendered on April 18, 2026. Cigna Healthcare denied the claim in full, citing CARC 151 ("Payer deems the information submitted does not support this many/frequency of services") and RARC N362 ("The number of days or units of service exceeds our acceptable maximum"), with the accompanying payer remark stating: "Units billed exceed the plan's allowable frequency for this service." MUSC Health respectfully disputes this determination. A single unit of CPT 99214 was billed for a single date of service, and the denial on frequency grounds is not supported by the facts of this claim.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Ms. Effertz is an 81-year-old established patient with a documented history of chronic sinusitis (onset 2007), hypertension (onset 1963), hyperlipidemia managed with Simvastatin, and prior episodes of viral sinusitis and acute viral pharyngitis. On April 18, 2026, she presented to MUSC Health Florence Medical Center, an on-campus outpatient hospital facility, and was evaluated by Amara J. Boone, NP (NPI 1203948576) for an acute upper respiratory infection (J06.9). Given her age, active chronic sinusitis, hypertension, and ongoing medication management, this encounter appropriately required medical decision-making of moderate complexity, consistent with the level of service billed.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial on frequency grounds is factually unsupported. CPT code 99214 was billed for exactly one unit on one date of service, April 18, 2026. There is no duplication, no repeat billing for the same date, and no pattern of excessive utilization evident in this claim. A frequency or utilization denial under CARC 151 and RARC N362 is applicable when the number of units or occurrences of a service exceeds a plan-defined threshold within a defined period. That standard cannot reasonably apply to a single unit of an evaluation and management service billed once on a single date of service.
Furthermore, the encounter itself was medically appropriate. Ms. Effertz is an 81-year-old patient with active chronic sinusitis and multiple comorbidities, presenting with an acute upper respiratory infection. An established-patient office visit at the moderate-complexity level is consistent with accepted standards of care for a patient of her age and clinical profile. The place of service (22, on-campus outpatient hospital) and the rendering provider's credentials are correctly reflected on the claim. The allowed amount of $198.50 already reflects Cigna's contracted rate acknowledgment, further confirming that the service itself is a covered benefit under the Cigna Healthcare Choice Plus plan, which remains active through December 31, 2026.
MUSC Health requests that Cigna review the claim data in its entirety. The record will confirm that no prior claim for CPT 99214 was submitted for this patient on this date of service, and that the single unit billed is the only unit that could logically be associated with one outpatient encounter. If Cigna's frequency edit was triggered by a system or data error, we respectfully request that the claim be reprocessed accordingly.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health requests that Cigna Healthcare reverse the denial of Claim MUSC-F1C0-1 and reprocess the claim for payment at the contracted allowed amount of $198.50. Supporting medical records for the April 18, 2026 encounter are enclosed with this appeal. Should Cigna require additional documentation or a peer-to-peer review, please contact our Revenue Cycle Appeals team promptly so that a response may be coordinated within the appeal deadline of November 14, 2026.

DEN-MUSC-F1C0-2.argument_summary: CPT 99214 is a standard covered E/M service; Cigna has cited no specific exclusion provision justifying denial for an established patient with active chronic conditions.
DEN-MUSC-F1C0-2.letter_text:
RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Kristie Effertz (MRN MUSC2132487), Claim MUSC-F1C0-2

Patient: Kristie Effertz  (DOB 1945-03-23)
MRN: MUSC2132487
Member ID / Group: CIG607831767 / GRP-43365
Claim number: MUSC-F1C0-2
Date of service: 2026-07-08
Procedure billed: CPT 99214 — Office/outpatient visit, established patient, moderate complexity
Primary diagnosis: J06.9 — Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified
Denied amount: $472.15
Denial code: CARC 204 / RARC N130 — This service/equipment/drug is not covered under the patient's current benefit plan.
Appeal deadline: 2027-02-04

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health is submitting this formal first-level appeal on behalf of patient Kristie Effertz (MRN: MUSC2132487, Member ID: CIG607831767, Group: GRP-43365) regarding the denial of claim MUSC-F1C0-2 for services rendered on July 8, 2026, at MUSC Health Rutledge Tower Ambulatory Care. Cigna Healthcare denied the claim in full — $472.15 billed — citing CARC 204 ("This service/equipment/drug is not covered under the patient's current benefit plan") and RARC N130 ("Consult plan benefit documents/guidelines for information about restrictions for this service"), with the payer remark stating: "Service is excluded under the member's plan benefit document." MUSC Health respectfully disputes this determination and requests a full reversal and payment at the allowed amount of $304.12.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Ms. Effertz is an 81-year-old established patient with a documented history of chronic sinusitis (active, onset 2007), hypertension (active, onset 1963), hyperlipidemia (active, onset 2002), and osteoporosis (active, onset 2015). She presented on July 8, 2026, for an outpatient office visit with rendering provider Amara J. Boone, NP (NPI 1203948576) at an on-campus outpatient hospital facility (Place of Service 22). The visit was coded as CPT 99214, an established-patient office or outpatient visit of moderate complexity, with a primary diagnosis of J06.9 (acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified). Given Ms. Effertz's age and her constellation of active chronic conditions — including hypertension, hyperlipidemia, chronic sinusitis, and osteoporosis — evaluation and management of an acute upper respiratory illness in this patient population appropriately supports the moderate-complexity level of service assigned.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial characterizes CPT 99214 as a non-covered service under Ms. Effertz's benefit plan. MUSC Health respectfully submits that this determination is inconsistent with the nature of the service provided and the coverage in force. Ms. Effertz's Cigna Healthcare Choice Plus plan carries a coverage period of January 1, 2024, through December 31, 2026, confirming active coverage on the date of service. CPT 99214 is a standard evaluation and management code representing a routine established-patient office visit — a category of service that is universally recognized as a core covered benefit under commercial health plans and is not, by its nature, a service type subject to categorical exclusion. MUSC Health has not received any plan benefit document, exclusion rider, or prior-authorization requirement from Cigna that would support the exclusion of outpatient evaluation and management services for this member. The payer's remark directs the provider to consult plan benefit documents, yet no specific exclusion language has been communicated to MUSC Health or the patient. A blanket denial citing a benefit exclusion, without identifying the specific exclusionary provision that applies to a standard E/M visit, does not constitute a sufficient or actionable denial under generally accepted claims adjudication standards. MUSC Health requests that Cigna identify, in writing, the precise benefit exclusion language relied upon to deny this claim. If no such exclusion applies to outpatient office visits of this type, the claim should be reversed and paid at the contracted allowed amount of $304.12.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that Cigna Healthcare conduct a thorough review of this appeal, identify any specific plan exclusion language upon which the denial is based, and reverse the denial of claim MUSC-F1C0-2. Payment of $304.12 — the allowed amount previously calculated by Cigna — should be issued promptly upon reversal. Should Cigna uphold the denial, MUSC Health requests a written explanation citing the exact benefit exclusion provision applicable to outpatient evaluation and management services for this member, along with information regarding the next level of appeal available under the plan and applicable state and federal external review rights.

DEN-MUSC-F1C0-3.argument_summary: A follow-up E&M visit for an 81-year-old with active, medicated hyperlipidemia and hypertension meets medical necessity; applying an LCD to a commercial claim is improper.
DEN-MUSC-F1C0-3.letter_text:
RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Kristie Effertz (MRN MUSC2132487), Claim MUSC-F1C0-3

Patient: Kristie Effertz  (DOB 1945-03-23)
MRN: MUSC2132487
Member ID / Group: CIG607831767 / GRP-43365
Claim number: MUSC-F1C0-3
Date of service: 2025-12-24
Procedure billed: CPT 99214 — Office/outpatient visit, established patient, moderate complexity
Primary diagnosis: E78.5 — Hyperlipidemia, unspecified
Denied amount: $457.71
Denial code: CARC 50 / RARC N115 — These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
Appeal deadline: 2026-07-31

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health is submitting this first-level appeal on behalf of patient Kristie Effertz (MRN: MUSC2132487, Member ID: CIG607831767, Group: GRP-43365) regarding the denial of claim MUSC-F1C0-3 for services rendered on December 24, 2025, by Daniel R. Okafor, MD (NPI 1558493021) at MUSC Health University Medical Center. The claim was denied on February 1, 2026, under CARC 50 ("These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer") with RARC N115, citing a Local Coverage Determination, and accompanied by the remark that "documentation submitted does not establish that the service was reasonable and necessary for the diagnosis reported." MUSC Health respectfully disagrees with this determination and requests full reversal and payment at the allowed amount of $251.85.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Ms. Effertz is an 81-year-old female with a well-documented, longstanding history of hyperlipidemia (ICD-10 E78.5), active since August 2002, and hypertension (ICD-10 I10), active since 1963. She has been maintained on simvastatin 10 mg continuously, with medication orders documented across multiple years and an active order placed September 15, 2020. Her lipid profile, recorded in September 2019, demonstrated a total cholesterol of approximately 190 mg/dL and triglycerides of approximately 187 mg/dL, findings consistent with ongoing dyslipidemia requiring active management. The December 24, 2025 encounter was a follow-up visit for this established, chronic condition, billed appropriately as CPT 99214 — an office or outpatient visit for an established patient of moderate complexity — at place of service 22 (on-campus outpatient hospital). The secondary diagnosis of J06.9 reflects a concurrent active condition also present in the patient's problem list.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial of medical necessity for a follow-up evaluation and management visit in an 81-year-old patient with decades-long, pharmacologically managed hyperlipidemia and comorbid hypertension is not supported by any reasonable clinical standard. Hyperlipidemia in a patient of this age and complexity requires periodic monitoring to assess medication efficacy, evaluate cardiovascular risk, and adjust the treatment plan as clinically indicated. CPT 99214 is appropriate for established patients presenting with conditions of moderate complexity, and the combination of active hyperlipidemia, active hypertension, and ongoing statin therapy in an elderly patient readily meets that threshold under standard evaluation and management coding guidelines.
Cigna's assertion that the documentation does not establish the service as reasonable and necessary does not account for the totality of the clinical record. The patient's active problem list, her continuous statin therapy, her documented lipid values, and her age-related cardiovascular risk collectively constitute a clear and compelling clinical rationale for a moderate-complexity follow-up visit. Furthermore, the invocation of a Local Coverage Determination under RARC N115 is inapplicable here, as LCDs are instruments of Medicare policy and do not govern commercial plan adjudication under the Cigna Healthcare Choice Plus plan covering this member through December 31, 2026.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that Cigna Healthcare reverse the denial of claim MUSC-F1C0-3 and issue payment at the previously established allowed amount of $251.85 for CPT 99214 rendered on December 24, 2025. We are prepared to submit the complete medical record for this encounter upon request and welcome a peer-to-peer review with Dr. Okafor should Cigna's medical director wish to discuss the clinical basis for this visit. This appeal is submitted within the deadline of July 31, 2026, through Cigna's designated appeal channels as required.

DEN-MUSC-F39B-1.argument_summary: Denial of a standard outpatient E&M visit for acute URI under an inapplicable LCD framework lacks clinical and contractual basis; full payment is warranted.
DEN-MUSC-F39B-1.letter_text:
RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Yi Weissnat (MRN MUSC8636135), Claim MUSC-F39B-1

Patient: Yi Weissnat  (DOB 2002-12-22)
MRN: MUSC8636135
Member ID / Group: UHC206518920 / GRP-81932
Claim number: MUSC-F39B-1
Date of service: 2026-06-24
Procedure billed: CPT 99214 — Office/outpatient visit, established patient, moderate complexity
Primary diagnosis: J06.9 — Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified
Denied amount: $1,080.46
Denial code: CARC 50 / RARC N115 — These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
Appeal deadline: 2027-07-20

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health submits this first-level appeal on behalf of patient Yi Weissnat (MRN: MUSC8636135, Member ID: UHC206518920, Group: GRP-81932) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-F39B-1 for services rendered on June 24, 2026, at MUSC Health Ashley River Tower by rendering provider Priya N. Raghavan, MD (NPI 1669504132). The claim was submitted on July 5, 2026, and denied on July 20, 2026, in the total billed amount of $1,080.46. UnitedHealthcare denied the claim under CARC 50 ("These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer") with RARC N115 ("This decision was based on a Local Coverage Determination (LCD)"), further stating that "documentation submitted does not establish that the service was reasonable and necessary for the diagnosis reported." MUSC Health respectfully disagrees with this determination and requests full reversal and payment of the claim.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Ms. Weissnat is a 23-year-old established patient with a documented history of acute viral pharyngitis, consistent with the primary diagnosis of J06.9 (Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified) reported on the claim. Her medical record reflects prior episodes of acute viral pharyngitis, prior throat culture, and prior antibiotic therapy, establishing a relevant clinical history for upper respiratory illness. The June 24, 2026, encounter was billed as two units of CPT 99214, an established outpatient office visit of moderate complexity, at Place of Service 22 (On Campus Outpatient Hospital), under revenue code 0510. The level of service reported is consistent with the evaluation and management of an acute respiratory condition in a patient with a known history of similar illness.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial characterizes the services as not medically necessary; however, the evaluation and management of an acute upper respiratory infection in an outpatient setting is a well-established, standard-of-care service. CPT 99214 is appropriately assigned when the medical decision-making or time requirements for a moderate-complexity established-patient visit are met. The diagnosis of J06.9 does not, in itself, preclude medical necessity; rather, medical necessity is determined by the clinical circumstances of the individual encounter, including the patient's presenting symptoms, history, and the complexity of the evaluation performed. Ms. Weissnat's documented history of recurrent acute viral pharyngitis and prior pharmacologic treatment supports the clinical appropriateness of a thorough evaluation at this visit.
Regarding the RARC N115 reference to a Local Coverage Determination, MUSC Health notes that LCDs are issued by Medicare Administrative Contractors and apply to Medicare fee-for-service claims. This claim involves a commercial HMO member covered under a UnitedHealthcare plan with a coverage period of January 1, 2024, through December 31, 2026. Application of an LCD framework to a commercial claim requires explicit contractual or plan-document authority. MUSC Health requests that UnitedHealthcare identify the specific coverage policy or contractual provision upon which this denial is based, as the invocation of an LCD in this context appears to be inapplicable. To the extent that UnitedHealthcare's internal medical necessity criteria were applied, MUSC Health requests that those criteria be disclosed so that a complete clinical response may be provided.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that UnitedHealthcare conduct a full clinical review of this appeal, reverse the medical necessity denial, and issue payment of the claim in accordance with the contracted allowed amount. Should UnitedHealthcare require additional clinical documentation, operative notes, or a peer-to-peer discussion with Dr. Raghavan, MUSC Health will promptly facilitate that process. We further request written notification of the appeal determination within the timeframe required under applicable state and federal prompt-pay and appeal-rights obligations. This appeal is submitted electronically via the Claims & Payments portal as directed in the denial correspondence, and MUSC Health reserves all further appeal rights pending the outcome of this reconsideration.

DEN-MUSC-FFD5-1.argument_summary: CPT 99214 is supported by the patient's multiple active chronic conditions elevating visit complexity beyond the acute J06.9 diagnosis; denial under CARC 11/RARC M64 should be reversed.
DEN-MUSC-FFD5-1.letter_text:
RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Renato Dare (MRN MUSC2558722), Claim MUSC-FFD5-1

Patient: Renato Dare  (DOB 1976-06-14)
MRN: MUSC2558722
Member ID / Group: SCD346795729 / GRP-86928
Claim number: MUSC-FFD5-1
Date of service: 2026-06-08
Procedure billed: CPT 99214 — Office/outpatient visit, established patient, moderate complexity
Primary diagnosis: J06.9 — Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified
Denied amount: $988.11
Denial code: CARC 11 / RARC M64 — The diagnosis is inconsistent with the procedure.
Appeal deadline: 2026-08-19

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health East Cooper Medical Center submits this formal first-level appeal on behalf of patient Renato Dare (MRN: MUSC2558722, Member ID: SCD346795729) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-FFD5-1 for services rendered on June 8, 2026, by rendering provider Sarah E. Whitmore, MD (NPI 1447382910). The claim was submitted on June 24, 2026, and denied on July 20, 2026, under CARC 11 ("The diagnosis is inconsistent with the procedure") and RARC M64 ("Missing/incomplete/invalid other diagnosis"), with the payer remark stating: "The diagnosis code reported does not support the procedure billed." The total denied amount is $988.11. MUSC Health respectfully contends that this denial is not supported by the clinical record and requests full reversal and payment at the allowed amount of $471.02.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Mr. Dare is a 50-year-old male with an extensive and active chronic disease burden documented in the medical record. His active conditions include type 2 diabetes with peripheral neuropathy, prediabetes, metabolic syndrome, hypertriglyceridemia, hyperglycemia, and anemia, all of which have been present and managed over a period of many years. He is an established patient currently maintained on extended-release metformin hydrochloride, a regimen that has been active since 2007. The June 8, 2026, encounter was billed as CPT 99214, an established patient office visit of moderate complexity, at Place of Service 22 (On Campus Outpatient Hospital). The primary diagnosis submitted was J06.9 (Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified), with a secondary diagnosis of R69. While J06.9 was the presenting complaint driving the visit, the patient's active chronic conditions — including diabetes with neuropathy, metabolic syndrome, and hypertriglyceridemia — represent significant comorbidities that directly bear on the complexity of medical decision-making required at this encounter.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial under CARC 11 and RARC M64 appears to rest on the premise that J06.9 alone is insufficient to support the level of service billed. MUSC Health agrees that J06.9 as a standalone acute diagnosis may not, in isolation, reflect the full clinical picture; however, the denial fails to account for the secondary diagnosis of R69 submitted on the claim, as well as the patient's well-documented active chronic conditions. CPT 99214 requires moderate complexity in medical decision-making, which encompasses the number and complexity of problems addressed, the amount of data reviewed, and the risk of complications. Mr. Dare's active diagnoses — type 2 diabetes with neuropathy, metabolic syndrome, hypertriglyceridemia, and anemia — represent multiple chronic conditions requiring ongoing management and directly elevate the complexity of any encounter, including one presenting with an acute upper respiratory complaint. An acute illness superimposed on poorly controlled or complex chronic disease is a recognized driver of higher-complexity evaluation and management services under current CPT guidelines. Furthermore, RARC M64 indicates that other diagnosis information was considered missing or invalid; the secondary diagnosis R69 was submitted and maps to active conditions in this patient's record, including hyperglycemia, metabolic syndrome, and hypertriglyceridemia. The clinical record supports the medical necessity and appropriate coding of the billed service.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that South Carolina Medicaid (Healthy Connections / SCDHHS) reverse the denial of Claim MUSC-FFD5-1 in its entirety and reprocess the claim for payment at the established allowed amount of $471.02. Should the Division of Appeals and Hearings require additional clinical documentation, operative notes, or a letter of medical necessity from Dr. Whitmore, MUSC Health will provide those materials promptly upon request. This appeal is submitted within the 30-day filing deadline of August 19, 2026.

RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Renato Dare (MRN MUSC2558722), Claim MUSC-FFD5-2

Appeal deadline: 2026-08-27

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health Florence Medical Center submits this first-level appeal on behalf of patient Renato Dare (MRN: MUSC2558722, Member ID: SCD346795729) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-FFD5-2 for a date of service of June 14, 2026. The claim was submitted on July 3, 2026, and denied on July 28, 2026, under CARC 11 ("The diagnosis is inconsistent with the procedure") and RARC M64 ("Missing/incomplete/invalid other diagnosis"), with the payer remark stating: "The diagnosis code reported does not support the procedure billed." The total denied amount is $420.93. We respectfully contend that this denial is not supported by the clinical record and that the claim should be reprocessed and paid at the allowed amount of $305.55.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Mr. Dare is a 50-year-old male established patient with a documented, active chronic disease burden that includes diabetes (ICD-10 E11.9, onset 2001), diabetic neuropathy (onset 2007), metabolic syndrome (onset 2007), hypertriglyceridemia (onset 2004), hyperglycemia (onset 2010), prediabetes (onset 2010), and anemia (ICD-10 D64.9, onset 2001). He carries an active medication regimen that includes extended-release metformin, initiated in 2007 for his diabetes. On June 14, 2026, Dr. Elena V. Castellanos, MD (NPI 1881726354), evaluated Mr. Dare at MUSC Health Florence Medical Center in an on-campus outpatient hospital setting. The primary diagnosis reported for that encounter was J06.9 (Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified), with a secondary diagnosis of R69. The service billed was CPT 99214, an established-patient office or outpatient visit of moderate complexity.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The payer's denial rests on the assertion that J06.9 does not support CPT 99214. This position does not accurately reflect CPT coding guidance. CPT 99214 is defined by the level of medical decision-making or time involved in the encounter, not by any single diagnosis code. An established patient with an acute presenting complaint such as an upper respiratory infection, evaluated in the context of multiple active chronic conditions including diabetes with neuropathy, metabolic syndrome, hypertriglyceridemia, and anemia, presents a clinical picture that routinely meets the threshold for moderate complexity medical decision-making. The management of an acute illness in a patient whose chronic conditions may affect treatment selection, drug interactions, and clinical course — for example, the use of antibiotic therapy in a diabetic patient with neuropathy and metabolic comorbidities — inherently involves a greater degree of clinical judgment than the same complaint in an otherwise healthy individual.
Regarding RARC M64, the secondary diagnosis of R69 was submitted on the claim and is supported by Mr. Dare's active documented conditions of hyperglycemia, metabolic syndrome, and hypertriglyceridemia, all coded to R69 in his longitudinal record. The diagnosis information submitted was neither missing nor invalid; it was present and consistent with the patient's known medical history. To the extent the payer requires additional specificity, the clinical record supports the submission as made, and any perceived coding gap does not negate the medical necessity or the appropriateness of the visit level.
South Carolina Medicaid's own coverage policies recognize that established-patient evaluation and management services are covered when medically necessary and appropriately documented. The encounter on June 14, 2026, meets that standard given Mr. Dare's clinical complexity.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that South Carolina Medicaid (Healthy Connections / SCDHHS) overturn the denial of Claim MUSC-FFD5-2, reprocess the claim, and issue payment at the previously determined allowed amount of $305.55 for CPT 99214 rendered on June 14, 2026. We are prepared to submit the complete encounter documentation upon request and welcome the opportunity to provide any additional information required to resolve this matter promptly.

DEN-MUSC-FFD5-3.argument_summary: Prior authorization is not required for routine established-patient E&M visits under SC Medicaid; the payer's own allowed-amount calculation confirms the service was covered and correctly coded.
DEN-MUSC-FFD5-3.letter_text:
RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Renato Dare (MRN MUSC2558722), Claim MUSC-FFD5-3

Patient: Renato Dare  (DOB 1976-06-14)
MRN: MUSC2558722
Member ID / Group: SCD346795729 / GRP-86928
Claim number: MUSC-FFD5-3
Date of service: 2026-06-06
Procedure billed: CPT 99214 — Office/outpatient visit, established patient, moderate complexity
Primary diagnosis: J06.9 — Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified
Denied amount: $495.45
Denial code: CARC 197 / RARC N54 — Precertification/authorization/notification/pre-treatment absent.
Appeal deadline: 2026-08-11

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health is submitting this formal first-level appeal on behalf of patient Renato Dare (MRN: MUSC2558722, Member ID: SCD346795729) regarding the denial of Claim ID MUSC-FFD5-3 for services rendered on June 6, 2026, by Robert K. Lindqvist, MD (NPI 1314059687) at MUSC Health Rutledge Tower Ambulatory Care. The claim was submitted on June 12, 2026, for CPT code 99214 (office/outpatient visit, established patient, moderate complexity), billed at $495.45. South Carolina Medicaid (Healthy Connections / SCDHHS) denied the claim in full on July 12, 2026, citing CARC 197 — "Precertification/authorization/notification/pre-treatment absent" — and RARC N54 — "Claim information is inconsistent with pre-certified/authorized services" — with the payer remark: "No prior authorization on file for the date of service billed." MUSC Health respectfully disputes this denial and requests full reimbursement of the billed amount.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Mr. Dare is a 50-year-old male with an extensive and active chronic disease burden managed longitudinally at MUSC Health. His documented active conditions include type 2 diabetes mellitus with peripheral neuropathy, prediabetes, metabolic syndrome, hypertriglyceridemia, hyperglycemia, and anemia. He has been maintained on extended-release metformin since November 2007. He also carries a history of recurrent acute upper respiratory infections, including prior episodes of acute viral pharyngitis and viral sinusitis, each coded under J06.9. The June 6, 2026 encounter was billed under primary diagnosis J06.9 (acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified) with a secondary diagnosis of R69, consistent with his concurrent metabolic conditions. Given the complexity of Mr. Dare's comorbid profile, the selection of a moderate-complexity established-patient visit level (99214) is clinically appropriate and well supported by the documented conditions requiring evaluation and management.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
South Carolina Medicaid policy governing outpatient evaluation and management services for established patients does not universally require prior authorization for routine office visits, particularly when rendered by an established treating provider in an outpatient setting. CPT code 99214, a standard established-patient office visit, is a widely recognized, non-invasive evaluation and management service. Prior authorization requirements under Healthy Connections are generally reserved for specific high-cost procedures, specialty services, or durable medical equipment as enumerated in the program's covered services guidelines — not for routine ambulatory E&M visits of this nature. DEN-MUSC-FFD5-4.argument_summary: CPT 99214 is supported by moderate-complexity decision-making given Mr. Dare's active chronic comorbidities; the denial misapplies CARC 11 and RARC M64 to an adequately documented encounter.
DEN-MUSC-FFD5-4.letter_text:
RE: Formal Appeal of Claim Denial — Renato Dare (MRN MUSC2558722), Claim MUSC-FFD5-4

Patient: Renato Dare  (DOB 1976-06-14)
MRN: MUSC2558722
Member ID / Group: SCD346795729 / GRP-86928
Claim number: MUSC-FFD5-4
Date of service: 2026-06-15
Procedure billed: CPT 99214 — Office/outpatient visit, established patient, moderate complexity
Primary diagnosis: J06.9 — Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified
Denied amount: $490.01
Denial code: CARC 11 / RARC M64 — The diagnosis is inconsistent with the procedure.
Appeal deadline: 2026-09-10

Dear Appeals Review Committee:

SUMMARY OF APPEAL
MUSC Health Florence Medical Center submits this formal first-level appeal on behalf of patient Renato Dare (MRN: MUSC2558722, Member ID: SCD346795729) regarding the denial of Claim MUSC-FFD5-4 for services rendered on June 15, 2026, by Sarah E. Whitmore, MD (NPI 1447382910). South Carolina Medicaid (Healthy Connections / SCDHHS) denied the claim in full on August 11, 2026, citing CARC 11 ("The diagnosis is inconsistent with the procedure") and RARC M64 ("Missing/incomplete/invalid other diagnosis"), with the payer remark stating: "The diagnosis code reported does not support the procedure billed." The billed amount is $490.01, with an allowed amount of $367.12 and zero payment issued. MUSC Health respectfully contends that this denial is not supported by the clinical record and requests reversal and payment at the allowed amount.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND
Mr. Dare is a 50-year-old male established patient with a documented, active chronic disease burden that includes type 2 diabetes with neuropathy, prediabetes, metabolic syndrome, hypertriglyceridemia, hyperglycemia, and anemia, all of which are recorded in his longitudinal medical record. He presented on June 15, 2026, at MUSC Health Florence Medical Center, an on-campus outpatient hospital facility (Place of Service 22). The encounter was billed as CPT 99214, an established patient office or outpatient visit of moderate complexity, with a primary diagnosis of J06.9 (Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified) and a secondary diagnosis of R69. Mr. Dare has a prior history of acute viral pharyngitis and viral sinusitis, both coded to J06.9, and his active comorbidities — including diabetes with neuropathy and metabolic syndrome — are well established in the record and directly relevant to the complexity of any acute illness evaluation in this patient.

BASIS FOR APPEAL
The denial under CARC 11 and RARC M64 appears to rest on the premise that J06.9 alone is insufficient to support a level-4 established patient visit. This position does not accurately reflect the totality of the clinical record. CPT 99214 is appropriately assigned when the medical decision-making or total time meets the threshold for moderate complexity. For an established patient carrying active diagnoses of type 2 diabetes with neuropathy, metabolic syndrome, hypertriglyceridemia, hyperglycemia, and anemia, an acute upper respiratory illness represents a materially more complex clinical evaluation than it would for a patient without such comorbidities. The management of an acute infection in the context of these active chronic conditions — including consideration of medication interactions with his current regimen of extended-release metformin and diphenhydramine — reasonably supports moderate-complexity decision-making.
Furthermore, the secondary diagnosis code R69 was reported on the claim and is associated in this patient's record with active conditions including hyperglycemia, metabolic syndrome, and hypertriglyceridemia. The payer's assertion that the other diagnosis is missing, incomplete, or invalid is inconsistent with the submitted claim data, which included R69 as a secondary diagnosis. To the extent the payer requires additional specificity, the clinical record supports the use of more granular codes for the active chronic conditions, and MUSC Health is prepared to submit a corrected claim with expanded secondary diagnosis coding if the payer determines that would resolve the edit.

REQUESTED ACTION
MUSC Health respectfully requests that South Carolina Medicaid (Healthy Connections / SCDHHS) reverse the denial of Claim MUSC-FFD5-4 and issue payment at the previously established allowed amount of $367.12 for CPT 99214 rendered on June 15, 2026. In the alternative, if the payer's clinical review team determines that additional diagnosis specificity is required to satisfy the coding edit, MUSC Health requests written guidance identifying the specific codes needed so that a corrected claim may be submitted without delay. This appeal is filed within the 30-day deadline established in the denial notice dated August 11, 2026, and is submitted in accordance with the Division of Appeals and Hearings' accepted procedures.
